requirement: Constructing a MultiplePiePlot with a non-null CategoryDataset registers the new plot as a change listener on that dataset, so that a dataset change fired on that dataset after construction results in the plot firing a change event (PlotChangeEvent) to all its registered PlotChangeListeners.

When BorderArrangement arranges a layout under a fixed-width AND fixed-height constraint (the arrangeFF path) and a right block is present, the right block is arranged with a width Range whose upper bound is the larger of (constraint width minus the arranged width of the left block) and 0.0; consequently, if the available width is so small that the left block already occupies all of it (or more), the right block's allowed width is clamped to a non-negative leftover (0.0) rather than being given a negative upper width bound, so the arrangement completes without throwing or placing the right block under a bogus negative-width constraint.
PiePlot.getMaximumExplodePercent() returns 0.0 (rather than throwing a NullPointerException by dereferencing the dataset's keys) when the plot's dataset is null.

getDataRange(ValueAxis) iterates over each non-null dataset mapped to the queried axis; when such a dataset has no renderer (getRendererForDataset returns null), the method must not throw a NullPointerException from accessing that renderer's annotations — instead it simply continues (no renderer-supplied annotations from that dataset are scanned/collected), and the computed range is derived only from the available data bounds.

When HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText needs to wrap text over multiple lines (i.e. the first line itself was wrapped) and the supplied nextLineTabStop is greater than or equal to the supplied width, the method must not throw an IllegalStateException and must still complete, producing a wrapped result instead of aborting.

Util.stripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes removes one leading and one trailing double quote and returns the interior text when (and only when) the input has length >= 2, begins with a double quote, ends with a double quote, and contains no double quote in the characters strictly between the endpoints (e.g. '"foo"' -> 'foo').

DefaultParser short-option recognition now matches a token against the FULL option name (the substring after a single leading '-', up to any '=' that separates an inline '=value') rather than only checking that the first character after '-' is a registered short option; consequently a token such as '-t1' or '-name=value' whose entire name is a registered (possibly multi-character) short/opt-name option is classified as an option.

When RemoveUnusedVars is run with removeGlobals=false, it does not remove/bare any formal parameters of functions it visits: unreferenced function arguments are left in place in every function declaration (the trailing-unreferenced-argument stripping step is skipped), and no call sites are modified for function-argument removal. Function-argument removal (peeling unreferenced trailing formals, and any call-site optimization of argument lists) occurs only when the pass is run with removeGlobals=true.

CommandLineRunner.createOptions() produces a CompilerOptions whose closurePass field is set to the boolean value of the process_closure_primitives flag; in particular, when --process_closure_primitives=false (or an equivalent false value) is supplied, options.closurePass is set to false, genuinely disabling the processing of Closure primitives such as goog.require, goog.provide, and goog.exportSymbol (the off setting is actually honored rather than being a no-op that leaves closurePass at its prior/default state).

In a function type clause of the form `this:` or `new:`, the context type may now be any basic type expression (e.g. array type, record/`{...}` type, union/`(...)` type, nested function type, `null`, `undefined`, or `*`), rather than being restricted to a plain type name; previously such context types caused the function type to fail with a generic type-syntax error.

In MaybeReachingVariableUse, when the ControlFlowAnalysis output is processed, a CFG node with an outgoing edge labeled Branch.ON_EX (a statement whose execution may be aborted into an exception handler) is treated as 'conditional', so a variable definition (a plain or compound 'x = ...' assignment, a 'var x = ...' initializer, or an assignment to the loop variable of 'for(x in ...)') located inside such a node no longer kills/removes the reaching uses of that variable that were present in the node's input lattice — the reaching uses entering such a node carry through it.

For a try statement with a finally clause, MinimizeExitPoints' exit-minimization does not remove or rewrite explicit exits (matching returns, breaks, or continues, per the current exitType/labelName context) that appear inside the finally block: statements within the finally clause are left unchanged by this pass.

The DIRECT_EVAL determination inspects the fully cast-unwrapped callee: a CALL whose callee, after removing any wrapping cast node(s), is a name equal to "eval" is annotated DIRECT_EVAL=true (on that inner eval name node); the presence of cast node(s) around an eval callee no longer prevents DIRECT_EVAL from being set.

When collapsing a statement body that is a block containing exactly one non-empty child, a child that is a FUNCTION declaration or a DO loop reached through one or more LABEL wrappers is still treated as a FUNCTION/DO, i.e. the braces around the labeled statement are retained rather than stripping to the bare labeled statement. Concretely the generator now emits e.g. `if(e1){A:function goo(){return true}}` from `if(e1)A:function goo(){return true}` and `if(x){A:do foo();while(y)}` from `if(x)A:do{foo()}while(y)` (previously the block would be stripped, producing the labeled FUNCTION/DO without its enclosing braces).

When a function body begins with one or more consecutive inner function declarations, the injected runtime parameter type-check statements are emitted after (following) those leading inner function declarations rather than at the very top of the body, preserving function-declarations-first ordering (e.g. `function f(i){ function g(){} }` with an annotated param `i` normalizes to `function g(){}` first and then the `jscomp.typecheck.checkType(i, ...)` statement).

The FlowSensitiveInlineVariables pass treats a property-deletion expression (`delete <expr>`, a DELPROP node) as a side-effecting operation for its inlining side-effect analysis, and consequently does NOT perform flow-sensitive inlining of a variable when such a `delete` expression occurs where the pass checks for side effects (in the sub-expressions on the right of the variable's def, in the sub-expressions on the left of the variable's use, or on the CFG path between a non-adjacent def and use); such candidate variables are left unmodified rather than replaced by their definition's value.

When the --version flag is supplied, CommandLineRunner writes a version banner to the configured error stream and flushes it, emitted before any help/usage output; the banner text is 'Closure Compiler (http://code.google.com/p/closure/compiler)\n' followed by 'Version: <ParserConfig.compiler.version>\n' and 'Built on: <ParserConfig.compiler.date>', where the two values are read from the com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.ParserConfig resource bundle.

When validating an implemented interface property of a constructor type, if the implementing instance type does have the property (instance.hasProperty(prop)) but the instance property's type — after restrictByNotNullOrUndefined — cannot be assigned to the interface's declared property type (also after restrictByNotNullOrUndefined), TypeValidator emits the HIDDEN_INTERFACE_PROPERTY_MISMATCH warning at the node (when shouldReport is true) with message format "mismatch of the {0} property type and the type of the property it overrides from interface {1}\noriginal: {2}\noverride: {3}", where {0} is the property name, {1} is the property's top-most defining type as returned by the interface constructor's getTopMostDefiningType, {2} is the required (interface) property type, and {3} is the found (instance) property type.

During reference collection within a scope, a NAME token whose string equals "arguments" is resolved to that scope's arguments Var (Scope.getArgumentsVar()) rather than to an ordinary declared variable looked up by name, so that occurrences of the bare identifier `arguments` (which is never an explicitly declared local variable) produce collected references keyed under the scope's arguments Var.

When scanning a candidate function's body for functions it refers to (used to decide inline/removal conflicts), InlineFunctions reports a referenced function name for a NAME that appears in `ID.call(...)` position at any depth of the body, in addition to plain `ID(...)` callee position; the reference even if not appearing as the direct callee NAME child of a CALL node is not missed.

Within a goog.scope(function(){...}) block, a reference to a name that is declared as a goog.scope-local alias (via `var name = <qualified-name-expression>`) is rewritten to that alias's fully-qualified initial value even when the reference textually precedes the alias's var-declaration statement in the block body (the full alias set of the block is discovered when the block's scope is entered, before contents are visited).

FlowSensitiveInlineVariables.process(externs, root) analyzes the program by traversing the externs root and the main AST root together as sibling roots sharing the scope rooted at their common parent, rather than by traversing the main root in isolation as its own scope root; as a side effect the externs tree is traversed within this common scope alongside the source (so free/extern references in function bodies are resolved against that scope).

During Compiler.initOptions, the GLOBAL_THIS diagnostic group's check level is set equal to options.checkGlobalThisLevel if and only if that checkGlobalThisLevel is on AND the GLOBAL_THIS diagnostic group is not explicitly disabled by the options' warnings guard (options.disables(DiagnosticGroups.GLOBAL_THIS) is false); in particular, when the GLOBAL_THIS group is explicitly disabled, initOptions leaves it disabled rather than forcing it back on to options.checkGlobalThisLevel.

AnalyzePrototypeProperties treats a chained prototype-property assignment of the form X.prototype.p = <value> (a simple '=' assignment whose LHS is a GETPROP chain of the form ...'.prototype.p') as a prototype-property assignment only when that assignment node is the direct child of a bare expression statement (it appears standalone, as in 'Foo.prototype.bar = function(){...};'). When such a chained prototype assignment occurs in some other syntactic position (its parent is not an expression statement, e.g. nested inside another statement or expression), it is no longer recognized as a prototype-property assignment, so the traversal does not analyze the assigned value within the context of the property p it defines.

When an assignment (including compound assignments such as += and -=) is transformed whose left-hand/target operand is not a valid lvalue (a node whose type is not one of NAME, GETPROP, or GETELEM), IRFactory reports an error with message "invalid assignment target", reported at the target node's line number.

When type-checking a CALL or NEW against a function type whose last formal parameter is a var_args ('@param {...T}') parameter, every actual argument that has no corresponding fixed declared parameter is type-checked against that var_args parameter's type rather than being silently skipped: once all fixed (non-varargs) declared parameters have been consumed, each remaining actual argument is still matched against the retained var_args parameter while arguments remain.

SetUniqueList.subList(fromIndex, toIndex) returns a SetUniqueList backed by a separately-allocated uniqueness Set of its own (not the same Set object the outer SetUniqueList uses), so that structural mutations made to the outer SetUniqueList after the subList is created (adding/removing elements outside the view) do not become visible in the returned sublist's membership checks.

The public static method UnmodifiableTrie.unmodifiableTrie declares Trie<K,V> (the general Trie interface) as its return type instead of the concrete UnmodifiableTrie<K,V>, so client code that statically expects an UnmodifiableTrie-typed result no longer compiles unchanged.

The serialized form of an UnboundedFifoBuffer written by writeObject now contains an int equal to the length of its internal buffer array (buffer.length), written immediately after the element-count int and before the per-element Object values.

Rebuilding ZipFile's entry-to-offset table during resolveLocalFileHeaderData re-registers every entry (with its OffsetEntry) in the same central-directory enumeration order regardless of whether that entry's name was changed to its Unicode form, so that no entry is lost, dropped, or reordered out of central-directory order by the reconstruction.

After getNextArEntry returns an entry, calls to read(), read(byte[]), and read(byte[],int,int) on the stream return at most the remaining unread portion of the current entry's declared content length; a read attempted at or beyond the end of the current entry's declared content returns -1 (EOF). Consequently bytes belonging to the archive's subsequent header/padding are never surfaced through the entry-content read path.

TarUtils.parseOctal throws IllegalArgumentException when an octal field contains no octal-digit content at all (i.e., after skipping leading spaces and trimming trailing NULs/spaces nothing remains); in particular a field consisting solely of space bytes now throws IllegalArgumentException rather than returning 0.

DeflateCompressorInputStream.matches(byte[] signature, int length) returns false when length <= 3; otherwise it returns true exactly when signature[0] equals byte 0x78 and signature[1] equals (byte) 0x01, 0x5e, 0x9c, or 0xda, and false otherwise.
X7875_NewUnix.getCentralDirectoryLength() returns a ZipShort whose value is 0 regardless of the current UID/GID settings, rather than reporting the same length as getLocalFileDataLength().

verifyCheckSum can propagate an IllegalArgumentException thrown by parseOctal when the trimmed CHKSUM-field content contains a byte that is neither an octal digit nor leading/trailing space/NUL padding (a field the previous lenient digit-scan never rejected) rather than merely returning false.

CpioArchiveOutputStream.close() closes the underlying (filtered) output stream and marks the stream as closed but does not write the CPIO trailing trailer entry; an archive that is closed without having previously called finish() is left unterminated, i.e. its produced bytes contain no CPIO trailer record.

TarUtils.parseName decodes each byte of the name field (up to the first NUL, or the end of the length-limited span) by appending to the result the character whose code point equals the byte's unsigned value (b & 0xFF), so that bytes with the high bit set (0x80 through 0xFF) produce characters U+0080 through U+00FF rather than being sign-extended (buggy version produced code points 0xFF80..0xFFFF for those bytes); ASCII bytes are unaffected.

Each invocation of CSVParser.iterator() on the same parser returns the same single CSVRecordIterator instance (not a newly created iterator), so a caller observing iterator identity sees the identical object across repeated calls.

CSVRecord.get(String name), when the name is present in the header mapping and its mapped index is out of bounds for the record's values array (an inconsistent record), throws an IllegalArgumentException whose message is of the form "Index for header '%s' is %d but CSVRecord only has %d values!" (with name, the mapped index, and values.length substituted), instead of letting an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException propagate to the caller.

When the adapter returned by TypeAdapters.newTypeHierarchyFactory(...).create(gson, typeToken) reads a JSON value whose decoded, non-null result is not an instance of the requested raw type (typeToken's raw type), read throws com.google.gson.JsonSyntaxException (whose message names the requested type and the actual runtime class of the decoded value) instead of returning the value.

JsonReader.nextLong() no longer throws IllegalStateException when the current token is an unquoted literal (peek state PEEKED_UNQUOTED); instead it reads the token's text as an unquoted value and attempts Long.parseLong on it, returning the parsed long when the parse succeeds.

When UnsafeAllocator.newInstance is invoked (via any of the reflection-based allocation strategies) with a Class argument that is an interface, it throws java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException (with message "Interface can't be instantiated! Interface name: <interface name>") instead of attempting to allocate an instance.

The single-quad hash function `calcHash(int q1)` re-mixes the intermediate hash after its high/low 16-bit fold: it additionally XORs the running hash with a copy shifted left by 3, then adds the high bits shifted right by 12. For each fixed (seed, q1) input this returns a different int hash value than the prior fold-only formulation, and consequently distributes single-quad (short, ~<=3-character) field names over differently-spread primary/subsequent slots, so that a seed that previously routed a run of small/colliding keys into one slot chain no longer does so.

When a release sanity check fails because a different, strictly smaller buffer is being released, the thrown IllegalArgumentException carries message text 'Trying to release buffer smaller than original'.

JsonGenerator.writeEmbeddedObject(Object) called with any non-null argument that is not a byte[] throws a JsonGenerationException whose message identifies the offending object's runtime class by name (rather than only a generic fixed message); in particular it no longer succeeds for unsupported embedded object types that are not null and not byte[].

When the parser delegate is constructed with allowMultipleMatches == false, traversal stops exposing content after a single accepted match: once one match has been accepted, subsequent candidate matches encountered during the parse (matched scalar values, and matched object/array values and path-included properties, whether reached through the normal nextToken() path, the offline _nextToken2 loop, or the buffered traversal loop) are not returned by the delegate.

When DefaultPrettyPrinter.createInstance() is invoked on an instance whose runtime class is a proper subclass of DefaultPrettyPrinter (i.e. a subclass that has not overridden createInstance), it throws an IllegalStateException whose message includes the text "Failed `createInstance()`:", the subclass's class name, and a phrase stating that createInstance must be overridden.

When the current node traversed by TreeTraversingParser is a TextNode whose text cannot be decoded under the Base64Variant passed to getBinaryValue(Base64Variant), the method propagates an InvalidFormatException for the broken Base64 content (it does not swallow the decode failure and return null).

JdkDeserializers.find(Void.class, ...) — i.e. resolution for the java.lang.Void target type — returns NullifyingDeserializer.instance (a non-null deserializer that discards/nullifies the JSON value to null) instead of returning null, so deserializing into a java.lang.Void type no longer falls through to reflective default construction of Void's private constructor.

When the String-collection property's ValueInstantiator exposes an array-delegating creator (via getArrayDelegateCreator/getArrayDelegateType), StringCollectionDeserializer.createContextual resolves and installs a delegate value deserializer for that array-delegate type, so that the later deserialize() call flows through the array-delegating createUsingDelegate path rather than the default-creation path.

DefaultDeserializationContext.findObjectId(id, gen, resolver) returns null instead of proceeding to build an IdKey / look up / create and return a ReadableObjectId when the supplied id argument is null — a null object id is never wrapped in an IdKey, looked up in _objectIds, or used to create/register a ReadableObjectId.
JavaType.isJavaLangObject() returns true if and only if the type's raw/erased class is java.lang.Object, and false for any other class (including subclasses like arrays, Strings, etc.).

MappingIterator.close() is an idempotent, terminal operation: the first call to close() closes the underlying parser (when one is present) and transitions the iterator into its closed state, after which subsequent close() calls, hasNextValue() calls, and nextValue() calls behave as on an exhausted iterator (no repeated access to a closed parser, hasNextValue() returns false, and nextValue() throws NoSuchElementException) rather than attempting further reads.

For an actual Map type (a java.util.Map implementation such as a class extending HashMap), the chosen serializer is, in order: a module-registered custom Map serializer if one matches, else an annotation-derived serializer (@JsonValue / JsonSerializable) if the class declares one, else the default Map serializer — so a module custom Map serializer overrides @JsonValue/JsonSerializable, and @JsonValue (e.g. a Map subclass whose @JsonValue method returns an int, serialized as that number) is still honored when no module serializer applies.

ShortSerializer.isEmpty(prov, value) returns true if and only if value is a Short whose numeric value is its zero ((short) 0); it returns false for any non-zero Short and for null (since the constant 0 Short is compared with .equals).

In ExternalTypeHandler._deserialize, when the buffered token stream for the external-type property begins with a JSON null value (JsonToken.VALUE_NULL), the method returns Java null immediately instead of merging the type-id and value into a wrapper array and invoking the property deserializer.

When StringArrayDeserializer deserializes via the custom value-deserializer path (i.e., a non-default String element deserializer is configured, after contextualization), each JSON null element (VALUE_NULL token) of the input array is resolved by invoking that element deserializer's getNullValue(), and the returned value (which may be non-null) is stored as that position of the result array, rather than the position always being Java null.

A TokenBuffer created via TokenBuffer(JsonParser, DeserializationContext) has BigDecimal forcing for buffered floats enabled exactly when the supplied DeserializationContext is non-null and has DeserializationFeature.USE_BIG_DECIMAL_FOR_FLOATS enabled; if the context is null or the feature is disabled, forcing is off.

JacksonAnnotationIntrospector.findNameForSerialization(Annotated), for a member that carries no @JsonGetter and no (explicit) @JsonProperty, treats a member annotated with @JsonBackReference, @JsonManagedReference, or @JsonUnwrapped as implying an implicitly-named serialization property: it returns PropertyName.construct("") rather than null (so that the member is still discovered as a serializable property whose name is resolved by default), just as members annotated with @JsonSerialize, @JsonView, or @JsonRawValue already are.

For the deprecated CollectionType.construct(Class<?> rawType, JavaType elemT): when rawType declares exactly one generic type parameter, the returned CollectionType exposes a single content binding mapping that parameter to elemT — observable via containedTypeCount()==1 with containedType(0)/containedTypeName(0) referring to the elemT type binding — whereas when rawType declares zero type parameters or any other count, the returned CollectionType exposes the empty type-binding set (containedTypeCount()==0).

When deserialize is invoked while the parser's current token is JsonToken.FIELD_NAME, the method consumes the entire enclosing object: it advances past the FIELD_NAME and repeatedly skips (discards) each value token it next encounters — the value bound to that field and the values of all following sibling fields of the same object — stopping only when nextToken returns null (end of input) or JsonToken.END_OBJECT, and then returns null without throwing. Observable consequence: parsing content after that enclosing object proceeds correctly because all of the object's content has been fully read/skipped.

TypeFactory.constructType(Type, JavaType contextType) returns the JavaType for the given type rather than throwing when contextType is null, resolving it with no binding context — i.e. the same result as constructType(type) (empty bindings).

In deserializeSetAndReturn (reachable via deserializeAndSet), when the parser's current token for the object-id-source property is a JSON null (JsonToken.VALUE_NULL), the method returns null immediately without invoking the value deserializer and without performing any readable-object-id lookup or item binding, and without decorating/binding the currently-being-deserialized instance.

BeanDeserializer._deserializeUsingPropertyBased no longer lets an UnresolvedForwardReference (raised while buffering/deserializing a regular, non-creator, non-object-id bean property value) propagate as a failure: instead of aborting, it continues consuming and processing the remaining fields of the current JSON object while recording the unresolved reference.

TypeBindings.asKey(rawBase) returns an object encoding both the given raw class and this bindings' type parameters such that two returned keys are equal (and hash-equal) iff they were created from the same raw class and from bindings whose type-parameter sequences are pairwise equal; keys created from different parameter sequences for the same raw class, or from different raw classes, are unequal.

For a bean property with inclusion ALWAYS/NON_NULL/default where SerializationFeature.WRITE_EMPTY_JSON_ARRAYS is disabled, empty values are suppressed (via BeanPropertyWriter.MARKER_FOR_EMPTY) when the property's effective serialization type — the type after refinement by @JsonSerialize(as=...) annotation override or static typing — is a container type, even if the property's declared field type is not itself a container type.

For a POJO whose type/class-level serialization inclusion is NON_DEFAULT (so that 'real' per-property defaults are in effect, per _useRealPropertyDefaults), when that POJO cannot be instantiated as a default bean (e.g. it has no accessible no-arg/default constructor), the affected properties are configured with null suppression, so a property whose value is null is omitted from the JSON output (a null field is not written), exactly as under the general/per-property NON_DEFAULT fallback handling.

CreatorCollector.addPropertyCreator records the supplied property list as the property-based creator arguments only when the offered property-based creator is actually adopted for the property-based slot (i.e. it replaces/becomes the stored C_PROPS creator). If the offered property-based creator is rejected by verifyNonDup in favor of an already-registered property-based creator, the previously recorded property-based arguments are left unchanged rather than being overwritten by the rejected candidate's properties.

The set of types that Jackson refuses to deserialize by default contains each of the following class names: com.sun.org.apache.xalan.internal.xsltc.trax.TemplatesImpl, org.apache.commons.collections.functors.InvokerTransformer, org.apache.commons.collections.functors.InstantiateTransformer, org.apache.commons.collections4.functors.InvokerTransformer, org.apache.commons.collections4.functors.InstantiateTransformer, org.codehaus.groovy.runtime.ConvertedClosure, org.codehaus.groovy.runtime.MethodClosure, and org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectFactory.

For a ResolvedRecursiveType whose self-reference has been resolved (setReference called), getSuperClass() returns the super class reported by the referenced type (i.e. the getSuperClass() of _referencedType), rather than returning null.

When _typeFromId is resolving a type id that contains '<' (a generic/canonical type id), if the JavaType produced by constructFromCanonical(id) is not a type-or-subtype of the raw class of _baseType, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown rather than that non-subtype type being returned.

ValueInstantiator.canInstantiate() returns true when canCreateUsingArrayDelegate() returns true, in addition to the pre-existing conditions (canCreateUsingDefault, canCreateUsingDelegate, canCreateFromObjectWith, canCreateFromString, canCreateFromInt, canCreateFromLong, canCreateFromDouble, canCreateFromBoolean).

When a class supplied in the parameterClasses varargs of constructParametricType is itself a generic type whose hierarchy resolution needs to walk its type variables, that parameter class is now resolved with empty (non-null) type bindings and must not throw a NullPointerException from unbound type-variable resolution (previously it was resolved with null bindings).

For an element whose content after its (possibly empty) attribute list consists of non-whitespace character/CDATA text immediately followed by a nested START_ELEMENT (true mixed content), XmlTokenStream returns the collected text as an XML_TEXT token — with that text exposed via getText() — rather than discarding the text and jumping straight to the nested element.

In Whitelist URL-attribute protocol validation (method testValidProtocol), when el.absUrl resolves to an empty string (the value could not be made absolute, e.g. unknown/custom scheme with no resolvable base), the attribute's own original value is used as the basis for the allowed-protocol prefix check instead of the empty string, so a link or URL attribute value that cannot be absolutized is not rejected (dropped as unsafe) for that reason alone — it is validated by its as-written value.

Entities.isBaseNamedEntity(String name) returns true exactly when name is a known entity belonging to the base entity set (such names decode without requiring a trailing ';'), and returns false for entity names known only in the extended/full set as well as for unknown names.

Parsing HTML that contains a self-closing start tag for a raw-data element (e.g. `<script ... />`) does not leave the tokeniser lexing in that element's data state, so any markup that follows it in the source is parsed normally — e.g. a `<div>` appearing right after `<script src='/foo' />` is produced as a discrete sibling element, not absorbed as raw/script text data continuing the element. Resulting DOM contains the self-closing element and normal sibling elements for the trailing markup.

When escaping with OutputSettings escape mode set to xhtml, a non-breaking space character (U+00A0) is emitted as the literal text ' ' (hex numeric character reference), rather than being appended as the raw U+00A0 character. This applies both in text-node and in-attribute escaping (the U+00A0 case is not guarded by the inAttribute flag).

When the tokeniser parses a doctype declaration whose after-name keyword is PUBLIC or SYSTEM (matched case-insensitively), the resulting Token.Doctype records that keyword as the canonical uppercase string "PUBLIC" or "SYSTEM" respectively, and getPubSysKey() returns it; when a doctype declares neither keyword (e.g. bare <!DOCTYPE html>), getPubSysKey() returns null.

Attributes.removeIgnoreCase(String key), when iterating attributes whose keys match key case-insensitively, removes (deletes from the Attributes set) at least one — and each — case-insensitively-matching attribute and completes normally without throwing a ConcurrentModificationException after removing an attribute during the iteration.

TokenQueue.chompBalanced(open, close) no longer silently returns the partially-consumed content when it reaches the end of the character queue before the nested delimiter group has been brought back into balance (depth > 0): it now fails by throwing an IllegalArgumentException instead of returning normally.

Element.hasClass(String className) resolves the class attribute by a case-insensitive match of the attribute name to "class", so that an element carrying its class-granting attribute under any letter-casing of that name (e.g. an attribute keyed "CLASS" or "Class") is still tested against its value: hasClass returns true exactly when className appears as one of that attribute value's whitespace-separated tokens (compared case-insensitively) and false otherwise, rather than behaving as if the class attribute were absent simply because no lowercase "class" key exists.

A self-closing start tag for an unknown/custom element (e.g. '<foo/>') does not produce the "Tag cannot be self closing" parse error, and the element is retained as self-closing so that it round-trips in serialized output with the trailing slash ('<foo/>').

When the parser is building a table section element (tbody, thead, or tfoot) - i.e. active/open-element context is within that table body, and a '<template>' start tag is parsed - the template element is inserted at the current position as a child of the section element that is currently open (and pushed onto the open-element stack without transitioning out), rather than being treated as non-table content and fostered out ahead of the table.

When parsing a 
 or  start tag in InBody insertion mode, a single line-feed character (U+000A, '\n') that immediately follows the tag in the source is consumed and discarded, so it is not emitted into the element and does not appear at the beginning of the element's text content (e.g. '
\nfoo
' parses the pre's text as starting with 'foo', without a leading newline).

A Tag stores an always-lowercased 'normal name' computed at construction from the tag name via Normalizer.lowerCase(tagName), and exposes it publicly through Tag.normalName(). The normal name is independent of the tag's output/stored name (which may preserve case), so an unknown tag whose stored name retains input case (parse with preserveCase) still reports its lowercase normal name.

Attribute.getValue() returns an empty string ("") rather than null when the attribute's stored value is null (as for a boolean attribute such as "hidden" parsed from HTML). Non-null values are returned unchanged.

NullPropertyPointer.createPath(context), in the non-attribute case, throws a JXPathAbstractFactoryException when the parent pointer is a NullPointer whose createPath returns a NullPointer equal to the original parent (i.e. the factory reported success but produced no distinct/null-realized object), instead of proceeding to delegate to newParent.createChild (which would recurse indefinitely).

When the right operand of an "=" / "!=" comparison (CoreOperationCompare.equal) evaluates to an InitialContext EvalContext, it is no longer collapsed to that context's single node pointer; instead the context is left in place (reset) so that the comparison iterates over the nodes the InitialContext selects, returning a match if any individual selected node value equals the left operand — e.g. a right variable holding a whole-collection/array is decomposed element by element rather than its composite value being compared wholesale against the left side.

When a non-null chars array is supplied to RandomStringUtils.random with start==0 and end==0, the generated string's characters are drawn only from within that chars array (index range [0, chars.length)); in particular this no longer overflows the array bounds (previously could select arbitrary near-Integer.MAX_VALUE indices causing ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException), and with a single-element chars set the deterministic result is the repeated char regardless of the letters/numbers flags.

The integer returned by translate is the number of input characters consumed, counting the optional terminating ';' only when a ';' immediately follows the consumed numeric digits: for an unterminated entity (no semicolon) the returned count omits the formerly-always-added 1, so e.g. a standalone '&#NNN' at end-of-input returns exactly its own full length; for a semicolon-terminated entity the semicolon is counted so the return is unchanged from before.

NumberUtils.createNumber rejects as invalid any input containing a '.' in which the exponent-marker position expPos (= str.indexOf('e') + str.indexOf('E') + 1) falls after the decimal point but exceeds the string's length (so expPos is not before decPos yet still past the end) by throwing NumberFormatException with message str + " is not a valid number." rather than throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException from str.substring(decPos+1, expPos).

indexOfAny(CharSequence, char[]) does not report a hit at the position of a cs character that is only a code-unit match: when cs's char at i is a high surrogate at a non-terminal cs position whose matching char in searchChars is a high surrogate at a non-terminal search position, indexOfAny returns i (the high surrogate's index) only if the immediately following code unit in cs equals the immediately following code unit in searchChars (i.e. the same supplementary character); otherwise it continues searching past i.

When the lower limit exceeds the string length and the effective upper limit would likewise reach or exceed the string length, abbreviate returns the whole (full-length, un-abbreviated) input string without appending the appendToEnd value, since capping lower to the string length leaves upper equal to the string length and no space is found at or beyond that index.

StrBuilder.indexOf(char ch, int startIndex) considers only indices from startIndex through the logical content boundary size-1 when searching, so it returns -1 (rather than a stale or beyond-content index) when ch does not occur within the logical content; it never reports a hit at an index >= size.

StrBuilder.indexOf(String str, int startIndex) bounds its forward scan using the builder's current logical size rather than the possibly-larger backing-array capacity: it only considers candidate start positions i for which the whole str would fit within the current content (i.e. it stops searching at size - strLen + 1). Consequently, whenever the internal character array has unused/stale slots beyond the current logical content (which arises naturally after the content shrinks, e.g. via deleteAll/deleteFirst/replace), the method returns -1 instead of returning a match index that lies at or past the current content end, and the deleteAll(String)/deleteFirst(String)/replaceAll(String,String)/replaceFirst(String,String)/contains(String) flows built on this indexOf no longer act on (or copy from) beyond-current-content positions.

As a result of the carry being keyed to real month lengths, a period spanning one or more complete calendar months (whose months may have differing/less-than-31 day counts) resolves into whole months plus a residual day count that is a genuine leftover within a real month, and is no longer further perturbed by a post-pass that re-normalized every field estimate by subtracting a reduceAndCorrect correction (those calls and the reduceAndCorrect helper have been removed).

When bounds are active, encode() maps each objective coordinate x[i] to x[i]/(boundaries[1][i]-boundaries[0][i]) rather than to (x[i]-boundaries[0][i])/(boundaries[1][i]-boundaries[0][i]); i.e. the normalized value no longer carries the lower-bound offset (so it is not shifted toward 0 by subtraction of the lower bound magnitude).

When a user-supplied convergence checker reports convergence during an iteration, doOptimize returns the best point (per goal) among the initial guess and every trial point evaluated across all iterations up to and including the current one — i.e. the globally best point encountered, not merely the better of the last two consecutive points (current/previous).

For the double-to-Fraction continued-fraction conversion, if the magnitude of the integer part `floor(value)` exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE (in particular for large-magnitude negative values such that floor(value) < -Integer.MAX_VALUE), a FractionConversionException(value, floor(value), 1) is thrown before the near-integer shortcut and before the iteration loop, rather than the conversion continuing and truncating out-of-range values into an incorrect int.

In computeGeometricalProperties, when getVertices() returns an empty loop array (v.length == 0), the region is reported as covering the whole space (getSize() = POSITIVE_INFINITY, barycenter = NaN) only if the underlying BSP tree has no cut (getTree(false).getCut() == null) and its root attribute is TRUE; in every other empty-loop case — including a degenerate/empty region whose BSP tree still has a cut node — getSize() is 0 and the barycenter is Vector2D(0,0).

When SimplexTableau.dropPhase1Objective scans the phase-1 objective row of non-artificial variable columns (from getNumObjectiveFunctions() up to the artificial-variable offset), it decides whether a column is a 'positive cost' column to be dropped by comparing that row entry to 0 with Precision.compareTo using the absolute comparison tolerance epsilon (this object's configured value), not a fixed ulps-based tolerance.

Complex.divide(Complex) returns Complex.NaN whenever the divisor equals Complex.ZERO (isZero), regardless of whether the numerator value is zero, finite non-zero, or infinite (NaN numerators are already separately handled earlier and also yield NaN).

When a REGULA_FALSI-configured secant solver is run and, during an iteration in which the new approximation does not cross onto the opposite side of the root (f1*fx >= 0, so the interval is NOT inverted), the computed approximation x equals the current upper bound x1, the solver immediately throws a ConvergenceException instead of continuing to iterate until the maximum number of evaluations is exhausted.

Vector3D.crossProduct returns Vector3D.ZERO (the null vector (0,0,0), without throwing) whenever the product of the two operands' squared norms (v1.getNormSq() * v2.getNormSq()) falls below the numerical-safety threshold MathUtils.SAFE_MIN, i.e. when one or both input vectors are of subnormally-small magnitude so that the naive computation would underflow or suffer catastrophic loss.

The no-arg GaussianFitter.fit() computes its starting guess via GaussianFitter.ParameterGuesser.guess() on the current observations and uses exactly that guess as the initial parameter vector passed to the underlying curve fit; the resulting fitted parameter array (norm, mean, sigma — norm first, from the fitted optimum, not merely the guessed norm) is returned.

The stop condition evaluated when processing a firing event is the disjunction (OR) of stop() across all registered event states at that event time, not just the currently firing state: if any handler requests stopping when its state is advanced to the event time, isLastStep becomes true and the integration terminates at that event time.

DiscreteDistribution.sample(int sampleSize) is declared to return Object[] (its erasure is Object[]), so the multi-sample result is always returned as a plain Object-array regardless of the type argument T.

In MultiDirectional.iterateSimplex, at the end of a while(true) pass in which the reflection step does not produce a point strictly better than the current best (so the reflection-improvement branch is not taken) and the contraction step also does not produce a point strictly better than the current best (so the contraction-improvement branch is not taken either), the method consults the configured RealConvergenceChecker, passing the current iteration count and, for each vertex index i in the simplex, calling checker.converged(iter, original[i], simplex[i]) comparing the vertex of the simplex as it was at the start of that pass (original) with the corresponding vertex of the simplex left by the contraction step; and if the checker reports convergence for every vertex, iterateSimplex returns immediately instead of beginning another pass of the loop.

UnivariateRealSolverUtils.bracket(function, initial, lowerBound, upperBound, maximumIterations) treats an expanded interval [a,b] on which f(a)*f(b) == 0.0 (i.e. at least one endpoint value is exactly zero) as a successful bracketing and returns the two-element array {a, b}, instead of throwing ConvergenceException.

In SimplexTableau.getSolution, when multiple decision-variable columns are basic within the same tableau row, only the lowest-indexed such column is assigned the row's RHS-derived coefficient; every later decision variable whose column shares a basic row already traversed for a lower-indexed decision variable is assigned coefficient 0, so each basic row contributes its RHS value exactly once.

When the passed invocation's method is a varargs method, each matcher whose list position corresponds to a fixed (non-vararg) argument position (positions strictly before the vararg) and that implements CapturesArguments has captureFrom invoked once with that invocation's fixed argument at that position.
DelegatingMethod.hashCode() returns the hash code of the wrapped java.lang.reflect.Method (rather than a constant), keeping it consistent with equals between equal DelegatingMethods.

MockitoCore.mock(Class, MockSettings, boolean shouldResetOngoingStubbing) now performs the reset of the in-progress ongoing-stubbing session on the mocking progress only when shouldResetOngoingStubbing is true; when the flag is false the mock is created without disturbing a current ongoing-stubbing session, so that a subsequent when()/stub() step (e.g. stubbing that was already in progress) can still be completed rather than being wiped out.

While mocks are being injected into a single @InjectMocks-annotated object (the per-@InjectMocks-instance candidate pool shared across that object's entire class-hierarchy walk), once a mock is successfully injected into one field of that object it is removed from the candidate pool, so the same mock instance is never injected into any other field of that same object — a single mock ends up in at most one of that object's fields.

During VerificationOverTimeImpl.verify's polling loop, an AssertionError thrown by delegate.verify(data) that is NOT a MockitoAssertionError (e.g. a plain java.lang.AssertionError or any AssertionError subtype other than MockitoAssertionError and the JUnit-flavoured ArgumentsAreDifferent) is no longer allowed to propagate immediately out of verify; it is now passed to handleVerifyException and thereby subjected to the recoverability/retry logic — i.e. stored as the accumulated error and, if the delegate can recover, slept/retried until the timer elapses (only then rethrown), rather than escaping from the very first polling iteration it occurs in.

When parseInto parses text that specifies some fields but omits the year (fields whose duration is between a month and a day, e.g. month-only or month/day), the default year given to the parse bucket — the year into whose context the parsed non-year fields resolve — is derived from the input instant's epoch millis getMillis() read via that instant's own chronology, NOT from its zone-offset-shifted local millis (instant.getMillis() + zone offset) and NOT in an override chronology/zone-selected context; consequently an input instant whose offset/local calendar year would fall one year away from its epoch-millis year (e.g. late-December UTC instants in a large positive-offset zone whose local time has already rolled into January of the next year) has its parsed year-defaulted fields resolved against the epoch year rather than the adjacent shifted year.

DateTimeZone.forOffsetMillis(int millisOffset) throws IllegalArgumentException (whose message includes the offending value) when millisOffset is outside the closed interval from -86,399,999 ms (-23:59:59.999) to +86,399,999 ms (+23:59:59.999), i.e. whenever its magnitude is at least a full day (86,400,000 ms); in-range millis offsets still resolve to the corresponding fixed-offset zone.
`pysnooper.pycompat` exposes a module-level boolean attribute `PY2` whose value is the logical negation of the existing `PY3` attribute (True on Python 2, False on Python 3).
Tracer.__init__ accepts a `custom_repr` keyword argument defaulting to the empty tuple `()`, so that @pysnooper.snoop(custom_repr=...) is a valid call without raising a TypeError.

get_write_function(output), when output is a str or a pycompat.PathLike, returns a callable that appends each string it is called with to a file opened at the path given by the output argument itself (rather than at the undefined name output_path, which raised NameError before the fix).
The env lookup resolves environment variable values from the controller process's ambient environment, using ansible.utils.py3compat.environ as the environment mapping.

For a collection requirement string whose parsed URL scheme is a non-empty value other than http/https (case-insensitive), _get_collection_info does NOT attempt a download; it takes the collection-name path instead (validating the name as a collection name).

The galaxy api module imports a urlparse callable that works on both Python 2 and Python 3, so that lib/ansible/galaxy/api.py imports successfully regardless of interpreter version (falling back from urllib.parse to urlparse).

Changing the vrf to a non-default value on an unconfigured device yields commands ['management api http-commands', 'no shutdown', 'vrf <vrf>', 'no shutdown'] (state command appears both before and after the vrf command).

CollectionRequirement._meets_requirements treats a requirement (in any form, including an operator form such as '>=0.0.1') against an installed version of '*' as satisfied — it skips that requirement rather than attempting a version comparison — when a parent is set and the requirement is not itself '*'.
In Driver._partially_consume_prefix, a tab character in the prefix advances the tracked indentation column by exactly 1, i.e. a tab is counted the same as a space rather than as 4 columns.

When gen_python_files_in_dir skips a symbolic link that points outside the root directory, it reports the skip via report.path_ignored(child, ...) using the message "is a symbolic link that points outside of the root directory".
prepare_input(src: bytes) exists as a module-level function and returns a 3-tuple of (newline, encoding, decoded_contents).

The `--- (original)` and `+++ (formatted)` labels produced by `format_file_in_place` in DIFF mode preserve the path spelling the caller passed in (e.g. a relative path stays relative), since the path is not resolved before being formatted into the diff headers.

Line.append_comment returns False without recording the comment when the line has no leaves (the comment would be first); in that case the comment's type is set to STANDALONE_COMMENT and its prefix is set to the empty string.
cookiecutter.exceptions defines a FailedHookException class that subclasses CookiecutterException, so it can be imported and caught by name.

When HTTPBearer is constructed with auto_error=False and the request lacks an Authorization header or lacks a scheme/credentials, HTTPBearer.__call__ returns None (this behavior is unchanged by the patch and is preserved for the auto_error=False configuration).

When multiple collected parameters share the same name, the entry kept is the last one encountered in the collected parameter order (its 'in', 'required', 'schema', 'description' and 'deprecated' fields win), rather than the first.

create_cloned_field, when cloning a ModelField whose type is a BaseModel subclass, produces a new model type whose __fields__ entries are themselves the result of create_cloned_field applied to each of the original model's fields (i.e. the cloned model's fields are recursively cloned rather than being the original model's field objects).

When a form (FormData) body is received, a non-body-typed Form parameter whose declared type is a plain (non-parametrized) sequence type — `list`, `set` or `tuple` — is populated with ALL submitted values for that parameter's alias, so a request sending the same field name multiple times yields every value rather than one single value.

request_validation_exception_handler builds its 422 response content by passing the error list from `exc.errors()` through `jsonable_encoder`, so the emitted JSON body is an encoding of that error list rather than the raw error list.
Calling update(x, new_x) returns a tensor whose value is the updated value of variable x (i.e. new_x when evaluated), rather than the raw assign op object.

keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence exposes a class attribute `use_sequence_api` set to True, so any instance of Sequence (including subclasses that do not override it) reports `use_sequence_api == True`.
The value returned by sparse_top_k_categorical_accuracy is a per-sample accuracy tensor of shape (num_samples,) (a mean over the last axis), with no reduction across samples.

sparse_categorical_accuracy accepts y_true of shape (num_samples, 1) (an extra trailing size-1 dimension) and produces correct per-sample results rather than throwing or broadcasting incorrectly; the label values are taken from the flattened y_true of shape (num_samples,), matching the shape of the per-sample argmax prediction.
Constructing StackedRNNCells with `reverse_state_order=True` emits a deprecation warning (via warnings.warn) while still constructing the object successfully.
Constructing a TimeseriesGenerator with a start_index+length that exceeds end_index (the effective start_index is greater than end_index) raises a ValueError; otherwise construction succeeds.
For a None/empty-input batch, fit_generator reports the callback batch log entry 'size' as 1 (the step-size used for data tensors).

On Python 3, text_to_word_sequence replaces every character in `filters` with the full `split` string before splitting, so that when `split` is multi-character the filtered characters are substituted by the whole split string, not by individual characters.

ImageDataGenerator.standardize no longer applies the generator's preprocessing_function to its input; standardize only performs rescaling/normalization (rescale, samplewise/featurewise center and std normalization, zca whitening) on the input it is given.

SimpleTaskState.get_necessary_tasks excludes tasks in UNKNOWN status from the returned necessary set: an UNKNOWN-status task with scheduler_disable_time None contributes neither its own id nor its deps, exactly as DONE and DISABLED tasks are excluded.

SimpleTaskState.set_status() does not apply the excessive-failures scheduler-disable path to a task that is already DISABLED: setting FAILED on a DISABLED task does not re-evaluate has_excessive_failures() for that call, so task.scheduler_disable_time is not set to a new timestamp and no 'DISABLED ... due to excessive failures' error notification is sent.

Instantiating a concrete BeamDataflowJobTask subclass whose dataflow_params is a DataflowParamKeys instance also runs the luigi.Task constructor (super().__init__()), so the constructed task is a fully initialized luigi.Task (e.g. task_id/task_family are populated) rather than a task on which luigi.Task.__init__ was never called.
luigi.interface.run called without an explicit cmdline_args argument (cmdline_args is None) does not raise an error and instead proceeds using sys.argv[1:] as the command-line arguments.
Constructing Worker(worker_id) without passing last_active results in worker.last_active being a numeric (float) epoch timestamp rather than None.

When run_job is invoked without SSH configuration and the job's jar() returns a falsy value (e.g. None or ''), it raises HadoopJarJobError with the message "Jar not defined" instead of attempting to check the path, and never calls os.path.exists on the jar value.

In the fallback (non-JSON) path, TupleParameter.parse returns tuple(literal_eval(x)), i.e. the ast.literal_eval result is coerced into a tuple, so any literal that evaluates to a non-tuple container (such as a bracketed list) is returned as a tuple rather than as that container type.

For an assistant calling get_work, RUNNING tasks whose capable-worker set is empty are excluded from the returned reply's 'running_tasks' list; RUNNING tasks with at least one capable worker remain included.

After applying inherits(TaskA) to a task class, instances of the decorated class expose a callable clone_parent method that returns self.clone(cls=TaskA, **args) with any passed keyword arguments forwarded.
_partition_tasks records a set_tasks['ever_failed'] status containing every task that has a 'FAILED' entry in the worker's task history.
SymLogNorm.__init__ accepts an optional keyword argument named `base` (positioned after `clip`), in addition to the existing linthresh, linscale, vmin, vmax, clip parameters.

Axis.set_view_interval / Axis.set_data_interval (the setters generated by _make_getset_interval for XAxis and YAxis) called with ignore=False on an axis whose current interval in the shared axes Limits object is inverted (i.e. its first entry is not less than its second entry) store the new interval as exactly (max(vmin, vmax, oldmin), min(vmin, vmax, oldmin)), where (oldmin, oldmax) is the current interval; the first (upper) entry is therefore derived from the current interval's first entry, not its second entry.
When the x-axis scale is not log (e.g. linear), non-positive limits passed to set_xlim are applied as given, with no substitution by the previous limits and no non-positive-limit warning.

pandas.melt() does not raise a KeyError for value_vars labels that are present in the DataFrame when the value_vars labels and the frame's column labels have mixed types (e.g. an integer column name listed alongside string column names); the presence check compares labels without coercing them to a common (string) dtype.

BinGrouper.recons_codes returns a list containing exactly one integer ndarray, whose value is 0 followed by every index i in the range 1 <= i < len(self.bins) for which self.bins[i] != self.bins[i-1], in ascending order (i.e. the positions of the non-empty (distinct) bin boundaries, always including position 0).

For a categorical Series input to .dt, the accessor's backing data preserves the category element dtype (e.g. datetime64[ns] or datetime64[ns, tz]) and all original elements, rather than being built from the Series of distinct categories.
AbstractHolidayCalendar.end_date defaults to Timestamp(datetime(2200, 12, 31)) (previously 2030-12-31).

BaseGrouper.agg_series, when the fast aggregation path `_aggregate_series_fast(obj, func)` raises a TypeError whose message string contains the substring "ndarray", does not propagate that TypeError; instead it falls back to and returns the result of `self._aggregate_series_pure_python(obj, func)`.

should_series_dispatch returns True when one of the two operands' first-column dtype is datetime64 and the other's first-column dtype is object, regardless of which operand holds the datetime64 dtype and which holds the object dtype (previously only the left-operand-datetime64 / right-operand-object ordering returned True).

When dispatch_to_series is called with `right` an ABCSeries whose dtype is exactly `timedelta64[ns]` and `axis == "columns"`, the per-column operand passed to `func` for column i is obtained from a numpy (positional) view of the Series rather than from `b.iloc[i]`, so that NaT entries retain timedelta semantics rather than datetime semantics.
In apply_empty_result, the reduction-inference probe invokes the apply function with exactly one argument, an empty Series (Series([])), and no additional positional or keyword arguments.

Calling `_with_freq(freq)` on a TimedeltaArray/DatetimeArray returns a distinct array object (a view sharing the same underlying data) instead of mutating the receiver in place; the receiver's own `freq` is left unchanged by the call.

In array_equivalent's strict_nan=True branch for string/object dtypes, comparing two corresponding elements that are themselves array-like (e.g. lists/ndarrays held in an object array) no longer raises ValueError from an ambiguous truth value of a multi-element boolean array; the elementwise comparison is reduced to a single boolean before being used as a condition.

For input containing no infinite values, `_Window._prep_values` may return the same array object it was given (no coercion/copy is forced just to handle infinities), so operations on the returned value preserve the original data and dtype.

DatetimeLikeArrayMixin.__add__ returns NotImplemented when other is a pandas Index (ABCIndexClass) instead of performing the operation itself, so the result is produced by the Index's reflected operation; concretely, for a TimedeltaArray tda, tda + dti equals tdi + dti for a DatetimeIndex dti = date_range('1999-12-31', periods=3), and tda + tdi equals tdi + tdi for a TimedeltaIndex tdi.

_get_grouper's label/level ambiguity validation honors the groupby axis: when the key is found in the object and validate is True, obj._check_label_or_level_ambiguity is invoked with axis=axis (the axis passed to _get_grouper), so for axis=1 a key that is both a column-level name and an index label is reported as ambiguous.

For a PeriodArray, _validate_insert_value's compatibility check raises IncompatibleFrequency (DIFFERENT_FREQ message) when the inserted Period's freq does not match the array's freq, rather than silently re-casting the Period to the array's freq.

Calling validate_baseindexer_support with the function name "count" does not raise NotImplementedError (only names outside the supported set {count, min, max, mean, sum, median, std, var, kurt, quantile} raise NotImplementedError).
The TypeError raised by Series.to_timestamp for an unsupported index carries the message "unsupported Type <name>", where <name> is the type name of the series' index.

When every date-unit attempt for the data raises (TypeError, ValueError or OverflowError), _try_convert_to_date returns the original unmodified data together with a failure indicator (False), so the caller treats the data as not date-convertible.

IntegerArray._values_for_argsort() does not raise (in particular not a ValueError from a minimum reduction on an empty selection) when the array has no missing values, including when the array is empty; it returns the copy of the underlying data unchanged.

assert_series_equal routes to the interval-specific comparison (assert_interval_array_equal on left.array/right.array) only when BOTH Series have interval dtypes; when exactly one Series has an interval dtype and the other does not, the interval branch is not taken and comparison falls through to a later dtype branch (ultimately the generic value comparison) instead of raising an 'Expected type IntervalArray' assertion from assert_interval_array_equal.

sanitize_array raises a TypeError with the message "Set type is unordered" when the data argument is a set (any collections.abc.Set instance, e.g. set or frozenset), instead of falling through to the catch-all cast path.

cartesian_product no longer coerces factors through pandas.core.common.values_from_object (the `import pandas.core.common as com` dependency is removed and the function still works for all supported inputs).
Rolling.corr(pairwise=...) on a dimension-1 object whose window is an offset (freq-type) rolling window does not select `self._get_window(other)`; the frequency-based window value is used instead.

The internal dispatch call made by `_Rolling_and_Expanding.apply` (i.e. `Rolling.apply` / `RollingGroupby.apply` / `Expanding.apply` / `EWM.apply` on this base) passes the caller-supplied `raw` value through as a `raw` keyword argument to `self._apply(...)`, so downstream `_apply` implementations can observe the same `raw` value that was passed to `apply`.

When `cols` is provided together with a list/tuple/ndarray/Index `header` of aliases, the length check compares the number of aliases against len(cols); writing succeeds iff len(header) == len(cols), and otherwise raises ValueError citing the cols-based column count.

When get_handle wraps an input file object in a TextIOWrapper, the newly created wrapper is not appended to the returned handles list if the underlying object is itself a BufferedIOBase or RawIOBase (only the wrapper for other kinds of objects is registered there).

When a TimeDeltaBlock's (or DatetimeBlock's) single stored value read by iget is an np.timedelta64 scalar, iget returns it wrapped as a pandas Timedelta instead of the raw np.timedelta64, representing the same duration.
The integer-extension-array handling in pandas.cut applies for all forms of bins: a scalar int, a sequence of bin edges, and an IntervalIndex all work with an integer-dtype extension array as x.

The exact-shape-match condition in Block.setitem continues to be: the right-hand-side array is at least 1-dimensional, its first dimension equals the (transposed) block values' first dimension, and its total size equals the block values' total size (unchanged predicate, now hoisted into a variable reused by both the categorical branch and the pre-existing astype branch).

Because _convert_axes routes index/column axis data through the same _try_convert_data helper, reading a JSON document whose axis labels require an int64 coercion that overflows also returns a result instead of raising OverflowError.

A replace call on a block whose match mask is empty does not take an early no-op shortcut: Block.replace still produces its result through the putmask-based replacement path (and, when convert=True, the post-replacement convert step) rather than returning the original block/its copy.

_get_empty_dtype_and_na returns, for the datetime upcast class, the NA value np.datetime64("NaT", "ns") (a datetime64[ns] scalar) rather than the integer iNaT sentinel, together with the dtype np.dtype("M8[ns]").
The TypeError raised by pivot() for a missing/None `columns` argument has the message "pivot() missing 1 required argument: 'columns'".

AsyncioServer.start_serving() raises NotImplementedError when the delegated call self.server.start_serving() raises AttributeError (i.e., when the underlying server object lacks start_serving / does not support it).

When the uri resolved by the router for the requested view name contains a "/" at a position greater than 0, url_for treats the substring preceding that first "/" as the route's host and removes it from the path, so the produced URL's path portion does not start with the host (e.g. a route uri of "example.com/foo" yields a URL whose path is "/foo").
is_gzipped(response) matches the Content-Type value case-insensitively, so values such as 'Application/GZip' or 'APPLICATION/X-GZIP' return True.

The idna fallback in _safe_ParseResult does not depend on the caller-supplied `encoding` parameter: the fallback applies the same way when canonicalize_url's except-UnicodeEncodeError retry is not triggered, so path/query/fragment percent-encoding still follows the passed `encoding` for URLs whose netloc fails idna encoding.
When a LocalCache has a falsy limit (None or 0), assigning items never evicts entries, so the number of stored keys grows without bound (all assigned keys remain retrievable).
After a robots.txt download error for a netloc, RobotsTxtMiddleware leaves an entry for that netloc present in its parser cache (set to None) instead of deleting the cache entry.

HttpProxyMiddleware._get_proxy encodes the 'user:password' credential string (both parts URL-unquoted when needed) into bytes before base64-encoding it, so the returned creds value is a bytes object equal to base64.b64encode(<bytes of 'user:pass'>).strip() rather than a base64 of a py2-str.

When a `<name>_BASE` setting exists, `_getcomposite(name)` builds the composite from the `<name>_BASE` entries and from those entries of `self[name]` whose stored priority is strictly greater than the 'default' priority; entries of `self[name]` whose priority equals 'default' are NOT included in the returned composite even though they are present in `self[name]`.

_iter_command_classes(module_name) enumerates the objects of each walked module via the plain values() view, so that calling it under Python 3 yields ScrapyCommand subclasses defined in each module instead of raising an AttributeError from a Python-2-only itervalues() call.

CrawlerProcess.__init__ passes the instance's normalized settings object (self.settings, a Settings instance) to configure_logging, so that a falsy/empty dict argument does not cause the root-logger handler setup inside configure_logging to be skipped (and so configure_logging never receives a raw dict from CrawlerProcess).

scrapy.utils.log exposes a function failure_to_exc_info(failure) that, given a twisted.python.failure.Failure instance, returns the 3-tuple (failure.type, failure.value, failure.tb) suitable for use as a logging exc_info value.

The deprecation warning emitted by Spider.start_requests is formatted to include, in '<module>.<classname>' form, the __module__ and __name__ of the concrete class of the spider instance on which start_requests() was called (i.e. the dynamic class, not always Spider).
_get_form_url(form, None), when the form element has no 'action' attribute, returns form.base_url unchanged (rather than attempting URL resolution on a missing action value).
The Errors class exposes an error code attribute named E175, whose value is the message template "Can't remove rule for unknown match pattern ID: {key}".

spacy.errors.Warnings.W022 can be resolved (no AttributeError) and, through the @add_codes wrapper, resolves to the warning message '[W022] Training a new part-of-speech tagger using a model with no lemmatization rules or data. This means that the trained model may not be able to lemmatize correctly. If this is intentional or the language you're using doesn't have lemmatization data, you can ignore this warning by setting SPACY_WARNING_IGNORE=W022. If this is surprising, make sure you have the spacy-lookups-data package installed.'

sudo.match returns False for a command whose script starts with the token `sudo` (command.script_parts non-empty and command.script_parts[0] == 'sudo'), regardless of whether the command's stderr or stdout contains any of the permission-denied patterns that would otherwise cause a match.

get_all_executables splits the PATH environment variable using os.pathsep as the directory separator (rather than a hard-coded ':'), so on a platform whose os.pathsep is not ':' (e.g. Windows, where it is ';') a PATH value like 'C:\a;C:\b' is treated as two directory entries and the executables found in both directories are returned (instead of treating the whole string as one non-existent directory path).

dirty_unzip.get_new_command builds the corrected command as '<original script> -d <archive name without .zip>', shell-escaping that destination directory via shells.quote, so a directory name containing shell-special characters is emitted quoted and remains a single argument; for ordinary names the output is unchanged (e.g. 'unzip foo' -> 'unzip foo -d foo', 'unzip foo.zip' -> 'unzip foo.zip -d foo').

The `cache`-decorated function (`thefuck.utils.cache`'s `_cache` wrapper) uses `contextlib.closing(shelve.open(cache_path))` as the `with` block's context manager, so the database returned by `shelve.open` is closed (its `close()` method called) when the cache read/write block exits, rather than requiring the shelve object itself to implement the context-manager protocol.

repr(CorrectedCommand(script, side_effect, priority)) produces the string 'CorrectedCommand(script={script}, side_effect={side_effect}, priority={priority})' with the three attribute values interpolated.

When the script contains no machine token (fewer than 3 space-separated tokens), get_new_command returns a single combined shell command joining 'vagrant up' with the original command, i.e. 'vagrant up && <original script>' without a trailing space before the separator.

When the script uses a longer launcher accepted by match ('xdg-open', 'gnome-open', 'kde-open'), get_new_command preserves that launcher verbatim and inserts 'http://' after it, e.g. 'xdg-open github.com' yields 'xdg-open http://github.com' (the launcher is not truncated or rewritten to 'open').

Fish.info() determines the shell version by invoking a single subprocess with the argument list ['fish', '--version'] (with stdout captured and stderr discarded), rather than running `fish -c 'echo $FISH_VERSION'`.

git_push.match returns True only when command.output contains the literal substring 'git push --set-upstream' (in addition to 'push' appearing in command.script_parts); an output that mentions 'set-upstream' without that full literal phrase (e.g. a successful push whose branch name contains 'set-upstream') does not match.

match() returns True only when command.output contains both the substring "fatal: A branch named '" and the substring "' already exists." (i.e. the closing single quote before " already exists." is required); for an output like "fatal: A branch named 'foo already exists." (no closing quote) match() returns False.

When an upstream option ('--set-upstream' or '-u') is present in command.script_parts at an index, get_new_command removes the argument at that index (the option itself) and then attempts to remove the element now occupying that same index; if that second removal fails because the index is out of range, it is silently ignored rather than propagating an IndexError.
RequestHandler exposes an overridable method `_break_cycles()` that, in its base implementation, sets self.ui to None; it can be called independently, not only from finish().

FacebookGraphMixin._on_access_token derives the session's access_token (and expires) entries from the access-token response body using the standard query-string parser (urlparse.parse_qs) rather than escape.parse_qs_bytes, so on Python 3 the resulting session values are native text strings rather than latin1-decoded byte strings.
The package data installed by setup.py includes the static test fixture file 'static_foo.txt' alongside the other tornado/test fixture files.

For a client-mode HTTP/1.1 request whose method is POST, PUT, or PATCH, which has no Content-Length header and whose Transfer-Encoding header is present with the exact value "chunked", HTTP1Connection.write_headers enables chunked output encoding (i.e. the body written is chunk-framed and finish() emits the terminating zero-length chunk) instead of treating the explicitly supplied Transfer-Encoding as an externally managed encoding.

IOLoop._ioloop_for_asyncio is a plain dict (not a WeakKeyDictionary) mapping asyncio event loop objects to IOLoop instances, so its entries persist until explicitly removed rather than expiring on garbage collection of the key.

If the function submitted to IOLoop.run_in_executor raises, the returned Tornado future is completed with that exception (the exception is propagated through the returned future rather than only being stored on the underlying concurrent future).

An instance constructed with disable=True and no explicit `total` stores `total` as its iterable's length when that is obtainable; e.g. tqdm([0], disable=True).total == 1, tqdm([], disable=True).total == 0, so bool() is True for a non-empty iterable and False for an empty one. When the length cannot be obtained (len(iterable) raises TypeError or AttributeError), the stored total is None.

get_elements_by_class, get_element_by_class, get_element_by_attribute, and get_element_by_id inherit the valueless-attribute tolerance, since they all delegate to get_elements_by_attribute (e.g. get_element_by_class('foo', '<e attr class="foo">x</e>') returns 'x').
When path is a bytes object that fails to decode as UTF-8, urljoin propagates the decoding error instead of returning None.

js_to_json leaves double- and single-quoted string literals unchanged by comment handling: a `//` sequence occurring inside a quoted string is not treated as a comment and the string is passed through the existing string-conversion path.

When the comparison value is treated as a string (either because the filter part explicitly gave a string value, or because the field's actual value is a string and the filter value is numeric), only the '=' and '!=' operators are allowed; any other comparison operator (<, <=, >, >=) raises ValueError('Operator %s does not support string values!' % op).

js_to_json converts the string content of a JavaScript string literal back to numeric form only when that content is entirely a hex or octal numeral (with optional trailing whitespace/colon); otherwise the literal is preserved/returned as a quoted string rather than being truncated to a numeric prefix (e.g. input content '07777abc' stays the string "07777abc" instead of becoming 4095).

_htmlentity_transform returns the literal string '&<entity>;' when the entity matches the numeric-reference form (#<digits> or #x<hexdigits>) but its codepoint is not a valid character (e.g. '&#2013266066;' yields '&#2013266066;'), instead of letting the chr() conversion's ValueError propagate (so unescapeHTML does not raise on such input).

FacebookIE still matches all URLs that matched before the change, including (a) URLs with no '#!' fragment at all such as 'https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?v=120708114770723' and (b) URLs whose pre-fragment prefix contains no '?' such as 'https://www.facebook.com/foo#!/video/video.php?v=123'.

unified_timestamp, when the input date string fails every date_formats() strptime pattern and is instead parsed by email.utils.parsedate_tz, now includes a 12-hour (43200-second) positive offset in the returned UNIX timestamp whenever the original input contains 'PM' (case-insensitive), so e.g. unified_timestamp('May 16, 2016 11:15 PM') returns the PM-corrected timestamp rather than the AM one.

astropy.utils.metadata.common_dtype returns a dtype representation that preserves the named fields (the resulting ndarray dtype's .descr, a list of (name, dtype-spec, shape) tuples) instead of the lossy .str void-form whenever the common dtype computed across the input arrays has named fields (i.e. arr_common.dtype.names is not None).

An Angle whose unit is specified as hours (u.hour or an hour unit that compares equal to u.hour) is normalized to hourangle, so that to_string() of such an angle (or when u.hour is passed as the to_string unit) yields hourangle/hms sexagesimal rather than being treated as a non-degree, non-hour-angle angular unit.

write_latex accepts a 'format' keyword argument of 'ascii.latex' in addition to 'latex' (previously any value other than exactly 'latex' was rejected), and for either accepted value it writes the LaTeX table output normally; a 'format' value other than 'latex' or 'ascii.latex' raises ValueError with the message "format must be 'latex' or 'ascii.latex', not {format}".

Constructing a TimeDelta whose val is a datetime.timedelta object (or iterable thereof) without an explicit `format` now succeeds, auto-selecting the 'datetime' format, rather than raising an error about only Quantities being usable.

biweight_midvariance of a constant (flattened, axis=None) input array, for which the median absolute deviation is 0, returns 0.0 instead of a NaN/inf result arising from division by zero (so biweight_scale of constant data returns 0.0).
