For a Media produced by summing other Media objects (m1 + m2 + ... + mn, in any nesting/grouping of the + operations), each CSS output medium's path list is built by merging that medium's paths across the css dictionaries of the base operands in their source addition order — a css medium appearing in any operand is present in the result, later-operand paths that duplicate earlier ones are not re-added, empty css members are inert, and parenthesization of the sum does not change any medium's resulting path list.

ModelChoiceField.to_python accepts a value that is already an instance of the queryset's model by extracting the value's to_field_name attribute (defaulting to the model's pk) and using that extracted value for the queryset lookup; this resolves to the cached DB object rather than raising an invalid_choice ValidationError as was the case when the model instance itself was passed as the lookup parameter.
When the UserCreationForm's model USERNAME_FIELD is present in self.fields, that field's widget renders with the attribute autocomplete="username" (in addition to its retained autofocus="").

Query.resolve_ref resolves a name present in the annotations via a single lookup and returns that annotation value, so an annotation whose stored value is present is returned and one that resolves against the model fields (not an annotation) continues through the joined-field/join_list rejection path unchanged.

In page_not_found, when the default 404.html template is unavailable (TemplateDoesNotExist for the default template name), the returned HttpResponseNotFound body is a complete HTML5 document that starts with '' and ends with '', with a containing "Not Found" and a containing "

Not Found

" followed by a

whose text is 'The requested resource was not found on this server.'

When settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS is non-empty, the Warning emitted for a duplicate db_table carries hint text "You have configured settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS. Verify that {comma-space-joined colliding model labels} are correctly routed to separate databases.", whereas when routers are not configured the report carries no hint.

The security.W019 deploy-check warning message text is changed: when XFrameOptionsMiddleware is present in MIDDLEWARE and X_FRAME_OPTIONS is not 'DENY', the reported warning now reads "You have 'django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware' in your MIDDLEWARE, but X_FRAME_OPTIONS is not set to 'DENY'. Unless there is a good reason for your site to serve other parts of itself in a frame, you should change it to 'DENY'." — it no longer contains the sentence "The default is 'SAMEORIGIN', but".

When a database connection's settings are prepared for testing, if the TEST sub-dictionary does not already specify a 'MIGRATE' key, that key is set to the default value True in the connection's TEST settings (in addition to the existing CHARSET/COLLATION/NAME/MIRROR defaults, which remain None).

When generating its result via reverse(), FlatPage.get_absolute_url() first attempts the candidate url self.url.lstrip('/') (self.url with all leading slashes removed) before the unchanged self.url, so that a stored url conventionally written with a leading slash (e.g. '/about/') is reversed with that leading slash removed (the '<path:url>' converter cannot begin with '/'); when such a url is reverseable, the returned URL reflects the stripped (no leading slash) form.

Query.set_group_by() treats an annotation's get_group_by_cols method as accepting the alias argument only if that method's signature declares a parameter named 'alias'. If it does declare such a parameter, get_group_by_cols is called as get_group_by_cols(alias=<annotation alias>); if it does not (including legacy methods that would absorb alias only via **kwargs), a RemovedInDjango40Warning whose text is '`alias=None` must be added to the signature of <module>.<qualname>.get_group_by_cols().' (module and qualname taken from the annotation's class) is emitted and get_group_by_cols() is called with no arguments. In both cases the returned group-by columns are merged into the query's GROUP BY clause.

Options.total_unique_constraints returns the list of objects in Meta.constraints that are UniqueConstraint instances whose condition attribute is None (i.e., unconditional/total unique constraints); UniqueConstraint instances with a non-None condition (partial constraints) and constraint objects that are not UniqueConstraint instances (e.g. CheckConstraint) are excluded from the returned list.

When a custom user model's USERNAME_FIELD is listed in its REQUIRED_FIELDS, the resulting auth.E002 checks.Error carries a non-None 'hint' whose text names the actual USERNAME_FIELD value (formatted with single quotes around it) and advises removing that value from 'REQUIRED_FIELDS'.

Each of Django's built-in signal singletons -- django.contrib.auth.signals user_logged_in/user_login_failed/user_logged_out, django.core.signals request_started/request_finished/got_request_exception/setting_changed, django.db.backends.signals connection_created, django.db.models.signals class_prepared/pre_init/post_init/pre_save/post_save/pre_delete/post_delete/m2m_changed/pre_migrate/post_migrate, and django.utils.autoreload autoreload_started/file_changed -- is now constructed without the providing_args argument, so importing these modules (which executes those definitions) and using the resulting signals never emits a RemovedInDjango40Warning.

MigrationLoader.__init__ accepts a replace_migrations keyword argument whose default value is True, so that MigrationLoader(connection) (and callers like MigrationExecutor) keeps the previous default collapsing behavior.

ModelMultipleChoiceField.__init__() emits a RemovedInDjango40Warning whenever the field's assembled error_messages still contain the deprecated 'list' key (e.g. supplied via the error_messages kwarg), and in that case copies the value of that 'list' override onto the 'invalid_list' key so the override still takes effect.
ModelState.clone() returns a ModelState whose .fields is again an order-preserving dict keyed by field name with the same name->field content.

When `loader.check_consistent_history(connection)` for a per-connection history check raises `django.db.OperationalError`, the `makemigrations` command no longer lets that exception abort execution; instead it catches it and continues to run to normal completion (conflict detection and onward), so the command does not exit with an error solely because a database connection could not be reached.

Every call to django.conf.urls.url(regex, view, kwargs=None, name=None) emits a deprecation warning whose category is RemovedInDjango40Warning (a subclass of PendingDeprecationWarning) and whose message text is 'django.conf.urls.url() is deprecated in favor of django.urls.re_path().'

The django.core.checks.Tags class provides a built-in tag member 'staticfiles' whose value is the string 'staticfiles', allowing system checks to be registered to, and filtered by, the staticfiles tag.

When an app module's default_app_config does not equal the auto-detected configuration and automatic detection found no configuration at all (app_config_name is None), the emitted RemovedInDjango41Warning message contains the text "However, Django's automatic detection did not find this configuration." rather than referencing a (None) picked configuration.

When update_fields names a field(s) not in the validated non-primary-key concrete-field set, Model.save raises ValueError whose message enumerates the offending fields as not existing, being m2m, or being non-concrete fields ('The following fields do not exist in this model, are m2m fields, or are non-concrete fields: <comma-separated names>') rather than the prior text that omitted the non-concrete-field clause.

When SessionBase.decode is given session data whose signing.loads decode raises signing.BadSignature AND whose legacy decode path (_legacy_decode) also raises an exception, decode does NOT propagate an exception: it logs a warning 'Session data corrupted' to the 'django.security.SuspiciousSession' logger and returns an empty dict {}.

call_command, when a required option or a member of a required mutually exclusive group is supplied via **options and that option's argparse action is one that stores a constant without taking an argument (store_true/store_false/store_const via _StoreConstAction, count via _CountAction, or append_const via _AppendConstAction), must pass it into the simulated parser as the bare option flag (e.g. '--flag') rather than '--flag=<value>', so the command executes instead of failing with an argparse parsing error/CommandError over an invalid '--flag=<value>' token.

Calling QuerySet.bulk_create() with an object whose concrete ForeignKey/OneToOne relation is cached (assigned) to an object that has no pk (obj.pk is None) raises a ValueError with message "bulk_create() prohibited to prevent data loss due to unsaved related object '<field name>'." instead of inserting the row.

When makemessages processes files whose translations cannot be assigned to a locale path (locale_dir is NO_LOCALE_DIR) but messages were produced, the raised CommandError message is: "Unable to find a locale path to store translations for file <normpath-of-first-build-file>. Make sure the 'locale' directory exist in an app or LOCALE_PATHS setting is set." (precisely, the message equals the concatenation given, i.e. there is a file path after 'file ' and the sentence is followed by the hint text).

ModelAdmin now defines the public method get_formset_kwargs(self, request, obj, inline, prefix), exposing a subclass-overridable point for computing the keyword arguments with which each inline formset is instantiated.

When dumpdata runs with --output on a path whose extension is '.zip' (always) or '.bz2'/'.lzma'/'.xz' while the corresponding compression module (bz2, lzma, lzma) is not importable, the fixture is instead written as plain text into a file at the output path with that extension stripped, and a RuntimeWarning is issued whose text names the unsupported extension (e.g. "Unsupported file extension (.zip)") and the actual file the fixture was saved to (the basename of that stripped path).
In get_connection_params, when settings NAME is None, the returned connection params set database to 'postgres' and do not forward any 'service' OPTIONS entry to psycopg2.

ExceptionReporter.html_template_path and text_template_path yield the paths of the builtin technical_500.html and technical_500.txt templates (resolved lazily via builtin_template_path) rather than via a module-level constant; technical_404_response and default_urlconf read technical_404.html and default_urlconf.html from the same lazily-derived builtin template directory.

django.utils.version no longer defines the module-level constants PY36 and PY37 (the minimum supported Python is now 3.8); third-party code that did 'from django.utils.version import PY36/PY37' will get an ImportError, while PY38 (and PY39) remain available.

On the SQLite backend, an exact-equality filter on a JSON member against one of the JSON literals true, false, or null (field__key=True / field__key=False / field__key=None) selects exactly the rows whose stored JSON value at that key equals that JSON literal, and does not additionally match rows storing a different JSON literal or an integer of equal SQL value, or rows lacking that key.

When binascii.Error data cannot be successfully decoded by the legacy fallback (e.g. the unsigned payload is not valid legacy JSON), CookieStorage._decode returns None and marks the storage as used rather than raising an exception.

django.db.models.fields.related.RelatedField.deconstruct() emits a `related_query_name` entry in its returned kwargs equal to the related_query_name value originally supplied to the field's constructor (snapshotted at construction in self._related_query_name), independent of any later change to remote_field.related_query_name, and omits the key when none was originally supplied.

When LocaleMiddleware.process_response() issues the 'add missing language prefix' redirect (404 response, no language prefix in path, i18n_patterns in use with modified/prefixed default language, and the language-prefixed URL or its trailing-slash variant is valid), the returned redirect response carries a Vary header that includes both 'Accept-Language' and 'Cookie' (in addition to any Vary fields already present on the redirect).

Field.check() performs a new system check (_check_db_comment) that, for a field with a non-empty db_comment referring to a database whose connection does not advertise supports_comments (and whose model does not require the 'supports_comments' DB feature), returns checks.Warning id 'fields.W163' stating the DB does not support comments on columns (db_comment).

When floatformat is given a string argument ending in the letter 'u' without a preceding 'g' (e.g. '2u', '-3u', 'u'), the formatted result is unlocalized: it uses the default '.' decimal separator and non-locale thousand separator rather than the active locale's separators. E.g. with the pl locale active, 66666.6666|floatformat:"2u" yields "66666.67". (Previously such an argument failed arg parsing and returned the repr of the input.)

When RelatedField._check_clashes() emits the 'fields.E302' Error (a reverse accessor name installed on the related model clashes with an existing field name on that related model, and the relation is not hidden), the Error message text exactly matches `Reverse accessor '{<related-model object_name>}.{<the accessor name>}' for '{<app_label.Model.field the defining field>}' clashes with field name '{<app_label.Target.field the clashing field>}'.` — i.e. the message begins by naming the actual reverse accessor being installed, qualified by the related model's object name.

In interactive superuser creation, when a REQUIRED_FIELDS option is supplied a non-None value via the command line (rather than being prompted), that value is validated by passing it through field.clean(value, None); if field.clean raises a ValidationError, the command terminates with a CommandError whose message is the ValidationError messages joined by '; ', rather than silently using the raw unvalidated value for the user.

prepare_lookup_value' accepts an optional third argument `separator` (defaulting to `','`); when the lookup key ends with `__in`, it splits the value string into a list on that separator instead of a hard-coded comma (e.g. prepare_lookup_value('x__in', 'a;b', ';') returns ['a','b']), so callers not supplying a separator still get the previous comma-splitting behavior and the __isnull handling is unchanged.

When HttpResponseBase.set_cookie is called with an 'expires' argument that is a datetime.datetime object (a naive datetime interpreted as UTC, or an aware datetime in any time zone) together with a non-None 'max_age' argument, it raises ValueError with message "'expires' and 'max_age' can't be used together." rather than silently computing max_age from expires and discarding the caller-supplied max_age.

Command.username_is_unique (a cached_property) returns True when the username field has unique=True OR some entry in UserModel._meta.total_unique_constraints has exactly one field equal to the username field's name (i.e., a single-field UniqueConstraint declaring the username field); otherwise it returns False. (A multi-field constraint that includes the username field does not make it return True.)

For an on_delete handler carrying the lazy marker (SET_NULL, SET_DEFAULT, or SET), the handler is invoked during collection even when its related-rows queryset would evaluate to empty; previously such handlers were only invoked when the related queryset was already non-empty/realized.

When transaction.mark_for_rollback_on_error's guarded body raises an exception while the target connection is inside an atomic block, the connection additionally records that same exception (in the connection's new rollback_exc slot) rather than only setting needs_rollback, so the raised exception instance becomes retrievable via connection.rollback_exc afterwards.

Supplying name (and optionally violation_error_message) as positional arguments to the constraint constructor, i.e. the legacy form BaseConstraint('name'[, 'message']), now emits a RemovedInDjango60Warning deprecation warning.

Constructing a Paginator without a supplied error_messages (or with error_messages=None) sets the instance's error_messages attribute to the default_error_messages dict, so the resulting Paginator error_messages always contains the three keys invalid_page, min_page, and no_results.

In the ModelAdmin system checks, a list_display item whose value (obtained via obj.model._meta.get_field(item) or via the fallback getattr(obj.model, item)) is a reverse one-to-many relation (a reverse foreign key, i.e. the field's .rel exists and field.rel.field.many_to_one is true) is rejected with a checks.Error carrying id 'admin.E109' whose message reads "The value of '<label>' must not be a many-to-many field or a reverse foreign key.".

When _save_parents re-encounters, along a second inheritance branch, a concrete parent that was already saved during the same save, the prior outcome for that parent (inserted vs. not) is reused so that a shared ancestor which had been inserted is still reported as having inserted parents (keeping the cumulative 'a parent was inserted' result true for the recursion), rather than losing knowledge of that earlier insert.

Figure(...) construction raises ValueError (with a message stating the size must be positive finite) when the figsize argument has any dimension that is non-finite or not strictly positive (i.e. zero or negative), so a figure whose width or height is 0 or negative is never successfully constructed.

A legend created with a string loc whose first space-separated token is 'outside' (e.g. 'outside upper left', 'outside upper center', 'outside upper right', 'outside lower center', 'outside lower right', 'outside lower left', 'outside right upper', 'outside right lower', 'outside left upper', 'outside left lower') is accepted: the 'outside' token is consumed and the remainder is mapped onto an otherwise valid standard loc value, so construction succeeds rather than failing as an unrecognized loc. The token order matters ('outside right upper' maps to a different resolved location than 'outside upper right').

For a mathtext ('$...$') marker, the marker's centering translation and size-normalization scale are derived from the curve-aware geometric bounding box of the mathtext text path obtained via Path.get_extents() (which returns the actual extent swept by the glyph outline Bézier segments, evaluated including curve extrema) rather than from the axis-aligned min/max span of the text path's raw vertices/control points.

When a ContinuousBase scale is set up with norming enabled (prop.normed True) and with norm endpoints needing unit conversion (values from the data min/max when norm is None, or from the explicit norm), converting those endpoints via axis.convert_units yields Python floats, so the resulting normalization constants a=forward(vmin) and b=forward(vmax)-forward(vmin) are float-scalar numerics. This ensures the scale's normalize step maps each data value's forward-transformed coordinate to a correct finite normalized value (the vmin value mapping to 0 and vmax to 1) rather than failing or producing invalid/non-numeric result types (such as numpy datetime/timedelta values) when the endpoints are date/time or otherwise non-float unit-converted values.

For a vector that is not entirely missing, variable_type determines the reported type from only the present (non-null) entries: it first returns 'numeric' only when every entry is missing; otherwise it removes all missing entries and then applies boolean detection and numeric/datetime/categorical inference to the remaining values. Concretely, an object/extension column that (ignoring nulls) is made up solely of numeric values is reported as 'numeric' rather than categorical, and one made up solely of datetime values as 'datetime', regardless of the presence/position of missing entries.

PreparedRequest.copy() produces a new PreparedRequest whose `_cookies` CookieJar is an independent copy of the source request's jar, so a copied request still carries (and an independent copy of) the cookies of the original.
PreparedRequest.prepare_method raises ValueError('Request method cannot be "None"') when given a method of None, rather than silently storing self.method as None.

HTTPAdapter.send catches a urllib3 ClosedPoolError raised by the connection operation and re-raises it as a requests.exceptions.ConnectionError (constructed from the original exception with request=request), rather than letting the raw urllib3 exception escape to the caller.

requests.exceptions defines a new exception class InvalidProxyURL, subclassing InvalidURL (and thus RequestException/ValueError), so that code can `from requests.exceptions import InvalidProxyURL` and catch it as an InvalidURL.

DataArray and Dataset (both subclassing common.DataWithCoords) each expose a `weighted(weights)` method that returns a weighted-operations accessor object constructed from the object under reduction and the provided weights (`DataArrayWeighted` for DataArray, `DatasetWeighted` for Dataset).

In the plain-text repr of a DataArray or Variable (array_repr), when display_expand_data is False the data is rendered as the single-line inline_variable_array_repr summary instead of the (possibly multi-line) short_data_repr value shown when the option is True or left at 'default'.

For each variable of the dataset, _protect_dataset_variables_inplace replaces the stored data with a CopyOnWriteArray wrapping of variable._data (itself wrapped in a MemoryCachedArray whenever the cache argument is truthy) exactly for those variables whose name is NOT a member of dataset._indexes; variables whose name IS one of the dataset's active indexes are skipped and left unmodified (their .data is never re-assigned).

When the global keep_attrs option resolves to True, the Dataset returned by a non-inplace binary operator (e.g. ds1 + ds2) has its dataset-level .attrs overwritten with the left operand's (self.attrs); when the option resolves to False (the default), the result's dataset-level .attrs are left as produced by _calculate_binary_op (i.e., not taken from the left operand).
When `--output <file>` is supplied and opening or writing the file raises an OSError, pylint prints the exception message to stderr and terminates with exit code 32.

Two BaseChecker instances are equal (×==× returns True) if and only if the string formed by concatenating the first checker's name and the string form of its msgs dict equals the analogous concatenation for the second checker; otherwise ×==× returns False. (Because the class defines no __eq__ prior to this patch and is decorated with @functools.total_ordering, this value equality also governs the total-ordering-derived comparisons, so checker ordering is now likewise based on this name+msgs value rather than object identity.)

Constructing a checker (an instance of BaseChecker or any of its subclasses such as BaseTokenChecker/BaseRawFileChecker) whose class sets a truthy `__implements__` attribute causes a DeprecationWarning to be raised with a message stating that using the __implements__ inheritance pattern for BaseChecker is no longer supported and that child classes should only inherit BaseChecker or the other checker types from pylint.checkers.

When _config_initialization finds unrecognized command-line options still left in the parsed argument list (entries beginning with '-' or '--'), it no longer raises _UnrecognizedOptionError (and hence no longer causes an uncaught exception traceback); instead it delegates to the linter's argument parser error handling (linter._arg_parser.error), which presents the parser's usage/error message on stderr and terminates execution (argparse's exit-code-2 behavior under its default settings) rather than propagating an exception.

In expand_modules, while resolving a target given by module name, only an ImportError is swallowed and recorded as a fatal error entry; a SyntaxError raised during that resolution is no longer caught, so it propagates out of expand_modules instead of being added to the reported errors.

If the same option source (a configuration file or the command line) supplies both an enable/disable option that covers 'all' (value with a comma-separated element exactly 'all') and the opposite all-action option — i.e. both an '--enable=all'-type/--enable for all and an '--disable=all'-type/--disable for all — pylint raises pylint.config.exceptions.ArgumentPreprocessingError with the message '--enable=all and --disable=all are incompatible.' instead of silently choosing an order.

When warn_explicit_for's internal warnings.warn_explicit call raises a Warning (i.e. the warning has been escalated to an error, e.g. via -Werror or warnings-as-errors), warn_explicit_for re-raises an exception of the SAME type as the raised Warning whose message string is the original warning message followed by the offending method's location, "\n at <filename>:<lineno>", where <filename> is inspect.getfile(method) and <lineno> is method.__code__.co_firstlineno.

_pytest.deprecated defines JUNIT_XML_DEFAULT_FAMILY as a PytestDeprecationWarning whose message is "The 'junit_family' default value will change to 'xunit2' in pytest 6.0.\nAdd 'junit_family=legacy' to your pytest.ini file to silence this warning and make your suite compatible."

_pytest.pytester_assertions.assert_outcomes: its `warnings` parameter is optional (default None); when it is None the assertion imposes no constraint on the actual warnings outcome count, and only when warned-parsed count is supplied explicitly (non-None) is the actual warnings count (parsed from the outcomes dict, defaulting to 0 if absent/not listed) required to equal it (mismatch makes the assertion fail).

The lazily re-derived `obj` value of a TestCaseFunction is the test method attribute obtained from the test class itself (i.e. an unbound method), in contrast to a bound method attached to a test-class instance; in particular the lazy lookup does not depend on, and does not need, the setUp-created TestCase instance (`_testcase`/bound `_obj`), so it still succeeds after `teardown()` has cleared those.

When a confcutdir C is configured, conftest discovery treats a directory D as within confcutdir scope (so an ancestor conftest can be collected for it) if and only if D is not one of C's own ancestor/parent directories; only a directory strictly above C (a proper ancestor of C) is out of scope. In particular the confcutdir's own directory, its descendants, and directories that are unrelated to it (neither ancestors nor descendants of C, such as a sibling subtree) are all within scope.

_load_imgs (the JPEG-decoding step behind fetch_lfw_people and fetch_lfw_pairs) decodes each face JPEG and, when resize is not None, resizes it using sklearn/externals/_pilutil's imread and imresize, i.e. PIL/pillow-driven helpers rather than lazily imported scipy.misc.imread/imresize, so that face decoding requires only that Pillow be installed and no longer depends on scipy.misc and no scipy.misc DeprecationWarning is emitted.

In precision_recall_fscore_support with average='binary' and a binary target whose only present label is the negative class (requested pos_label is absent, so the positive class has zero true positives and zero true/predicted samples), the function no longer short-circuits to a silent literal (0., 0., 0., 0) tuple; instead it proceeds through the normal support/divide computation with labels=[pos_label], so the ill-defined positive-class metrics are reported as 0.0 and an UndefinedMetricWarning is raised rather than the call returning a hard-coded all-zero tuple with no warning.

When the true targets scored are of type 'continuous-multioutput' (multi-column continuous y), calling score first emits a FutureWarning whose message states that the default value of multioutput (not exposed in the score method) will change from 'variance_weighted' to 'uniform_average' in version 0.23 to keep consistent with metrics.r2_score; when the targets are single-output continuous, no such FutureWarning is emitted.

Passing a discrete_features string that is not 'auto' (or that is not ExactlyEqual to the literal 'auto') raises a ValueError with message 'Invalid string value for discrete_features.', instead of being treated as a boolean-like or index-like value.

kmeans_plusplus now exposes a new keyword-only parameter `sample_weight` (array-like of shape (n_samples,), default None, versionadded 1.3); when provided it is validated against X via _check_sample_weight (a malformed weight — e.g. negative values or length != n_samples — raises), and non-None weights are propagated into the private weighted seed-selection routine.

RocCurveDisplay.plot renders a legend at location 'lower right' whenever a label is present in the main ROC line's kwargs OR in the chance-level line's kwargs (so that when plot_chance_level=True the 'Chance level (AUC = 0.5)' line is always included in the legend); it renders no legend only when neither curve carries a label.

When fitting an AdaBoost* estimator whose estimator is not set and whose base_estimator is set to None, a FutureWarning is emitted whose message states that 'base_estimator' was renamed to 'estimator' in version 1.2 and will be removed in 1.4 (i.e. an explicitly-provided None base_estimator is treated as a deprecated use of the base_estimator parameter).

In BaseForest.fit, the unavailable-target check that raises ValueError ('The type of target cannot be used to compute OOB estimates...') for an OOB-unsupported y (multiclass-multioutput or unknown) is performed only when oob_score is set AND either new estimators were grown this call or the estimator lacks an oob_score_; a warm_start refit that grows no new trees on an already-OOB-computed estimator never raises this ValueError regardless of the supplied y's target type.

Both MLPClassifier and MLPRegressor accept a new `max_fun` constructor keyword argument (with default 15000) which is stored as the public instance attribute/estimator parameter `self.max_fun` and forwarded to the shared BaseMultilayerPerceptron initializer; it is visible through the estimator's parameter interface (get_params).
The man builder registers a confval named 'man_make_section_directory' whose default value is False.

A new Sphinx configuration value `autodoc_typehints_description_target` is registered with a default value of `'all'`, restricted to the two allowed values `'all'` and `'documented'` (Sphinx's enum validator rejects any other value), and flagged as an upgrade/rebuild-triggering setting.

When the napoleon_use_param config option is enabled, the content of a 'Receives'/'Receive' section is rendered as docutils field-list roles, producing a ':param NAME:' description and, where a type is present, a ':type NAME: <type>' line for each parameter; comma-separated co-declarations (e.g. 'x, y: int') are split into separate :param:/:type: groups.

When the linkcheck extension is set up (module setup()), the 'linkcheck-process-uri' event no longer registers rewrite_github_anchor as a handler, so github.com hrefs/fragments are no longer rewritten to prefix their fragment with 'user-content-' during hyperlink collection/checking; a github.com URL such as '.../sphinx#documentation' is collected and checked under its original fragment rather than being rewritten to '.../sphinx#user-content-documentation'.

The C domain DefinitionParser accepts as fundamental type specifiers the remaining GNU/standard-extension scalar keywords: the decimal '_Decimal32'/'_Decimal64'/'_Decimal128'; the integers '__uint128', '__int128', and (optionally 'signed'/'unsigned'-prefixed) '__int(8|16|32|64|128)'; and the floating/profile extensions '__float80', '_Float64x', '__float128', '_Float128', '__ibm128', '__fp16'.

Every pending_xref node produced by type_to_xref now carries a refspecific attribute (its value is True exactly when the incoming target began with a leading '.', and False otherwise); because PythonDomain.resolve_xref treats mere presence of the refspecific attribute as enabling refspecific search, all type-annotation cross-references emitted through type_to_xref (e.g. from py:data/py:attribute/py:property ':type:', function return/parameter annotations) are now resolved in refspecific search mode (module/class-context and suffix-based lookup) rather than the default exact-match mode even when the target is not prefixed.

When factorint(n, multiple=True) yields a factorization in which an entry has non-positive multiplicity (a case reachable only when n's inputs introduce denominator primes, e.g. factor-rich Mul/dict composite inputs), that entry is represented in the returned list by S(1)/p repeated |multiplicity| times rather than by an integer p; otherwise positive-multiplicity entries remain integers p.

An Add that is a pure complex 'number' r + i*I with r, i rational and with D = sqrt(r^2 + i^2) rational (a Pythagorean triple) evaluates a Rational power whose denominator (q) is 2 (e.g. the square root) to the closed principal-branch algebraic form sqrt((D - r)/2)^p * ((D + r)/abs(i) + sign(i)*I)^p (with the p-th power of the inner binomial expanded), rather than remaining an unevaluated radical; e.g. sqrt(3 + 4*I) yields the exact reduced value.

Mod.eval reduces Mod(p, q) when the dividend p is a Mul containing at least one inner Mod factor whose divisor equals the outer divisor q: it folds the remaining non-Mod factors of p into the Mod, returning a product equal to Mod(net, q) where net is the product of the non-Mod factors multiplied with the product of the dividend arguments (args[0]) of all of p's inner Mod factors. E.g. Mod(a*Mod(b,q), q) reduces to Mod(a*b, q) (non-mod factor a moved onto inner dividend b), given the inner divisor matches q.

The sinc class no longer subclasses TrigonometricFunction; sinc is instead a direct subclass of Function. Consequently a sinc(...) instance is not an instance of TrigonometricFunction (whereas previously sinc(x).__class__ was a TrigonometricFunction with sinc being a sinc instance), while it remains an ordinary Function/Expr.

When logcombine collapses a group of log terms sharing a common coefficient factor k into the single logarithm log(combined), where combined is produced from the same logcombine routine over the product of the terms' (coefficient-raised) arguments, that resulting single logarithm is constructed with automatic evaluation disabled, so that it is stored back into the combination table in an unevaluated form rather than already auto-simplified; this prevents the intermediate combined log from being prematurely evaluated (for instance when the grouping reduces to a form involving numeric/log content that autoevaluation would absorb or alter) before the opposite-signed-coefficient division recombination of the same pass can act on it.

When JuliaCodePrinter prints a Mul whose factors include a Pow with exponent exactly -1 whose base is itself a Mul holding more than one factor, the Julia division denominator text for that base (which uses elementwise './' 'as appropriate') is wrapped in parentheses so that the denominator product is grouped rather than left as a bare product after the division operator.

In the unicode path of _print_BasisDependent, when reassembling a newline-containing coefficient, the branch that re-inserts the basis vector label is chosen by which parenthesis glyph the stripped coefficient text contains: if it contains the `\N{right parenthesis extension}` glyph (a vertically-extended/fraction-height rendering), the label is inserted exactly once immediately after the first occurrence of that glyph (the loop breaks after the first insertion), instead of being duplicated after every parenthesis hook on every line of the tall rendering.

The differential operator text used is '∂' (partial) when requires_partial(e) is true and otherwise the total-differential value ('ⅆ'); the same operator selection applies consistently to the numerator and to every denominator operator as determined by the current hunk's unified 'd' variable.
Contains(x, s).as_set() raises NotImplementedError instead of returning the Contains object itself.

A new physical constant named `elementary_charge`, with symbol/abbreviation "e", of electric-charge dimension (`charge`), and numeric scale factor `1.602176634e-19 * coulomb`, is defined and exported from the `sympy.physics.units` namespace (accessible as `u.elementary_charge`).

When IndexedBase is constructed from a string label together with assumptions passed as keyword arguments, the Symbol stored as the resulting label (args[0] / label property) is created with exactly those assumptions, so the label itself carries the assumption set (e.g. IndexedBase('A', real=True).label.is_real is True and the label is the Symbol 'A' with the real assumption).

latex() accepts a new optional boolean keyword argument parenthesize_super, defaulting to True, and forwards it into the LatexPrinter configuration; the LatexPrinter's default settings likewise define parenthesize_super to True (so a printer constructed without that setting also behaves as True).

SciPyPrinter._print_airyai maps a SymPy airyai function to the string 'scipy.special.airy(<printed arg>)[0]', where <printed arg> is the printer's rendering of the function's single argument (index 0 of scipy.special.airy, corresponding to Ai).

Range.is_finite_set evaluates to True for a Range whose start and stop are both known integers (covering concrete integer bounds and integer-valued symbolic bounds), i.e. every bounded integer range is reported finite regardless of its step or size.
dup_zz_mignotte_bound returns the non-negative even integer bound; for the polynomial `f = x**3 + 14*x**2 + 56*x + 64` over the integer domain ZZ it returns exactly 152.

collect(expr, syms, evaluate=False), when syms contains a nonsymbol (an expression that is neither a Symbol nor -Symbol nor contains a Wild), returns a dict in which each value (the collected coefficient/Add expression for a key) has had the internal Dummy placeholders substituted back to the original input symbols, i.e. the coefficient values are expressed in terms of the caller's original syms/expr symbols and contain no leaked temporary Dummy variables. (Keys were already mapped back before this change; now values are mapped back too.)

The purestr representation of a MatrixSymbol built from a string name remains reconstructible: purestr(MatrixSymbol('x', 2, 2)) yields the exact code string 'MatrixSymbol(Str('x'), Integer(2), Integer(2))' whose eval equals the original MatrixSymbol (mirroring the documented behavior of dotprint/srepr output after the Str conversion).

In LatexPrinter._print_Pow, when the expression is a Pow whose base is a commutative Rational unit-fraction (base.p * base.q == abs(base.q)) and whose negative rational exponent is not -1, the LaTeX emitted is \frac{1}{(\frac{p}{q})^{m}} where p,q are the base's stored numerator/denominator and m is the absolute value of the negative exponent (e.g. rendering Pow(Rational(1,2), -2, evaluate=False) as '\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2})^{2}}'), rather than routing through _print_Mul.

When Factors is constructed from an Expr whose power decomposition already has an entry keyed by the imaginary unit I and whose commutative argument list also contains standalone I atoms (whose count i was removed from the args), the resulting I entry in the factors dict is the sum of the pre-existing I-entry exponent and i — the pre-existing I exponent is not clobbered/replaced by i.

When the domain of a DDM is a RealField (RR) or ComplexField (CC), DDM.rref selects each pivot by row-pivoting within the column: among the not-yet-processed rows it chooses the one whose entry has the largest absolute value, using that row as the pivot row before continuing with the standard elimination; matrices over these inexact fields are therefore reduced correctly and the returned reduced-row-echelon form and pivot list match a properly row-pivoted RREF rather than picking an accidentally small leading entry as the pivot.
LaTeX printing of a single-argument LambertW raised to a power produces the exponent as a superscript attached to the W symbol: W^{n}\left(z\right) where n is the printed exponent.

When a denominator-only unevaluated Mul has exactly one denominator factor, the printed numerator is the literal '1' and the result takes the single-factor form '1/<denominator>' (no enclosing parentheses); when it has more than one denominator factor the result takes the multi-factor form '1/(<d1>*<d2>...)' with parenthesized denominator.

For f an instance of Min or Max containing the decomposition symbol, when every symbol-containing argument of f has a decompogen whose trailing elements (all elements after the first, after an argument that itself yields exactly one decomposition element is treated as if it decomposed as [symbol, arg]) are mutually identical, decompogen(f, symbol) returns [Min_or_Max_same_type] + [that common trailing sequence], where the rebuilt Min/Max preserves the same type (Min stays Min, Max stays Max) and the same positions/values of symbol-free arguments, with each symbol-containing argument position replaced by the first element of that argument's own decompogen.

pow_rep_recursive, when asked to select exactly one more term (k == 1) to complete the remaining amount n_remaining, resolves that final term directly instead of recursing further: it emits the tuple terms + (r,) where r is the exact p-th integer root of n_remaining, and emits that tuple only if n_remaining is an exact p-th power (r^p == n_remaining) and r <= n_i; if n_remaining is not an exact p-th power or its exact root exceeds n_i it yields nothing, and in every k == 1 case the generator returns immediately rather than descending more recursion frames for that term.

_format_float(value) always returns a string of length at most 20: when the base representation exceeds 20 characters and contains scientific notation ('E'), only the leading mantissa characters are dropped so the retained prefix plus the intact 'E' exponent portion totals 20 characters; when the base representation exceeds 20 characters and contains no 'E', the first 20 characters are returned.

HttpResponseBase.make_bytes, given a memoryview argument, returns the underlying raw bytes of the memoryview (equivalent to bytes(value)) instead of encoding the memoryview's str() representation in self.charset.

In django.utils.numberformat.format, the zero-normalization applied to Decimals smaller than the decimal_pos cutoff discards the sign: a Decimal with magnitude below the cutoff produces the unsigned string (e.g. format(Decimal('-1e-200'), '.', decimal_pos=2) yields '0.00' with no leading minus), because the value is reset to a positive Decimal zero before the sign/negative handling.

When running the psql subprocess via runshell_db, if conn_params contains a truthy 'sslmode' value, the subprocess environment (passed as env= to subprocess.run) has its 'PGSSLMODE' variable set to str(sslmode); if the parameter is absent or falsey, 'PGSSLMODE' is not injected into the environment.

URL resolution through regex-based patterns (re_path/url, via RegexPattern.match) excludes from the resolved kwargs any named capture group whose value is None (i.e., an optional named group in the regex that did not participate in the match). Such an unmatched optional group no longer appears as a keyword argument with value None; it is dropped from the match's kwargs entirely.
EnumSerializer.serialize() returns the imports set {'import <module>'} for the enum member's module, without including any imports that serializing the member's underlying value would require.

During the same Model._check_ordering relation-path walk, once a path segment resolves to a field that is not a relation, the walk no longer treats any subsequent segment as a field of the model owned by the enclosing relation path (in the buggy code _cls kept that model and a later segment matching one of its real field names was silently accepted); a further segment after a non-relation field is now acceptable only if it resolves as a registered transform/lookup of that non-relation field, and if it cannot, that ordering entry produces an E015 error.

Calling str() on any member of a Choices-derived enum class (Choices itself, IntegerChoices, TextChoices, or a user subclass) returns the string form of that member's value (str(member.value)) rather than the standard enum string form that names the member, e.g. 'MyEnum.MEMBER_NAME' or the enum class reference.

Assigning a value to the pk attribute on a multi-table-inheritance (concrete-parent) model instance, in addition to setting the instance's own local primary-key attribute, also sets the instance attribute for the remote (parent) pk of every parent link registered in _meta.parents whose field is not the model's own primary-key field to that same assigned value. Non-parent-linked, single-table models are unaffected: pk assignment still only sets the local pk attribute.

Every Choices class created through ChoicesMeta — including Choices, IntegerChoices, TextChoices, and any user-defined subclass of these — gets a class attribute 'do_not_call_in_templates' whose value is True (i.e. it is set when the class is created, not merely inherited through MRO lookup).

During model setup for a subclass with parents but no declared explicit primary key, promoting the selected parent field to be the model's primary key no longer raises ImproperlyConfigured('Add parent_link=True to <field>.') when that field's remote_field.parent_link is not True.

ModelChoiceField: When a ModelChoiceField uses a RadioSelect widget but the field does allow blank (blank argument is True), the leading empty/blank choice is retained (empty_label stays equal to the supplied empty_label, defaulting to '---------'), so an empty radio option is still rendered.

When autodetecting changes, if a newly created model's base is given as a dotted string 'app.Model' and that base model is present in both the from_state and to_state project states, and the base model has removed a field (the field name is present in the old base model state's fields but not in the new base model state's fields) whose name is also redeclared among the newly created model's own fields, then the generated creation is made dependent on the removal of that same-named base field (a removed-field dependency on (base_app_label, base_model_name, field, False)).

SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias returns True for a delete whose query references only its model's base table (exactly one alias has a nonzero refcount once the base table is ensured present), even when the base-table alias's stored alias_refcount would otherwise be zero because all query-time references had been released; only when additional join aliases are also active does single_alias evaluate to False.

ExpressionWrapper.get_group_by_cols(alias=None) delegates transparently to its wrapped inner expression, returning self.expression.get_group_by_cols(alias=alias). As a result, when an ExpressionWrapper is included in GROUP BY processing it contributes exactly the GROUP BY columns that its wrapped inner expression contributes (e.g. none when the inner expression is a bare constant Value, because Value.get_group_by_cols() returns []), rather than the wrapper expression node itself being treated as a GROUP BY column.

SessionBase._legacy_encode returns an ASCII string that is base64-encoded content of hash.encode() + b':' + serialized, where serialized is self.serializer().dumps(session_dict) and hash is self._hash(serialized); the resulting string is in the legacy format consumed by _legacy_decode.

On POSIX systems, locks.lock() returns False (does not raise) when the flock call fails with BlockingIOError, i.e. when a non-blocking (LOCK_NB) lock attempt is denied due to contention; exceptions other than BlockingIOError propagate.

OutputWrapper.flush() delegates to the flush() method of the wrapped stream (self._out) when that stream has a flush attribute, and does nothing (neither raising nor forwarding) when it does not — so that calling flush() on an OutputWrapper no longer raises (as the previously inherited io.TextIOBase.flush behavior did) and instead flushes the underlying destination stream.

Q.deconstruct() no longer special-cases a single non-Q child by re-encoding it into keyword kwargs: for a Q built from a single lookup keyword (single two-element child, e.g. Q(name='x')), the child is now returned as an element of the positional args (args=(('name','x'),)) with an empty kwargs dict, rather than as args=() with kwargs={'name':'x'}.

BaseDatabaseOperations.year_lookup_bounds_for_date_field gains an optional iso_year keyword flag; when iso_year=True the returned [lower, upper] pair spans the ISO-8601 week-numbering year equal to value, not the calendar year value — the lower bound is the day on which ISO week 1 of value begins, and the upper bound is the last day of that ISO week-numbering year (the day before ISO week 1 of value+1 begins), each still passed through the same date-value adaptation used by the calendar path.

URLValidator raises a ValidationError (message 'Enter a valid URL.', code 'invalid', params {'value': value}) when the value is a str that contains any tab ('\t'), carriage-return ('\r'), or line-feed ('\n') character, and this rejection happens even when the same value would otherwise have been accepted by the trivial regex or by the IDN retry path.

settings_to_cmd_args_env() resolves the database name for the mysql CLI from settings_dict['OPTIONS']['database'] when present, falling back to settings_dict['OPTIONS']['db'] and then to settings_dict['NAME'] (i.e. the OPTIONS 'database' key is now accepted as an alias); when the resolved value is non-empty it is appended as the final positional (database) argument in the returned command args.

BoundWidget.id_for_label returns the value of the 'id' key in the subwidget's data['attrs'] dictionary, i.e. the id attribute that will actually be rendered on that option/input; when data['attrs'] contains no 'id' entry (e.g. the form has auto_id disabled and the widget's own attrs specify no id), it returns None rather than fabricating an id string from the widget name and index.

When the value being serialized by TypeSerializer (via serializer_factory / MigrationWriter.serialize) is exactly the models.Model class type (identity match in the special_cases list), the serialization result is the string 'models.Model' with the import set {'from django.db import models'}, so that this import is propagated into the writer's imports and a generated migration referencing models.Model (e.g. as a CreateModel base) ends up importing models from django.db.

When BaseFormSet.full_clean() runs and no formset-level ValidationError is caught (including when the formset is unbound / management form is invalid / all checks pass), the non-form error list it produces and that formset.non_form_errors() returns is an ErrorList whose error_class is 'errorlist nonform', so rendering it as HTML (as_ul()/str()) emits '<ul class="errorlist nonform">'.

modelformset_factory(model, ...) accepts an `edit_only` keyword argument that defaults to False, and the FormSet class it returns exposes a class attribute `edit_only` whose value equals the `edit_only` argument passed in.

The `to_field` keyword is added only to relations classified as ForeignKey; when a relation column is classified as OneToOneField (unique or primary-key), no `to_field` keyword argument is added to the generated output even if the referenced column is not the referenced table's primary key.

The base Field class exposes a per-field-class attribute `non_db_attrs` (a tuple of attribute names whose change does not affect a column definition and thus is ignored when deciding whether a field alteration is needed). Its default value includes blank, choices, db_column, editable, error_messages, help_text, limit_choices_to, on_delete, related_name, related_query_name, validators, and verbose_name; standard field subclasses inherit it. A custom field subclass may override/extend `non_db_attrs` to declare which of its deconstruct keyword attributes are non-schema-affecting.
The --check option help text states that it exits with a non-zero status when model changes are missing migrations and that it does not actually write the migration files.

get_aggregation decides whether to route the aggregate through the subquery-wrapping path based on whether existing annotations actually involve aggregate/window computation: it uses a subquery only if some existing selected annotation contains an aggregate or an OVER clause, or if some existing filter references an aggregate/window alias (a HAVING/QUALIFY condition); the mere presence of pre-existing annotations that are neither is no longer sufficient to force a subquery.

A constraint whose `violation_error_code` is not None is deconstructed (and thus cloned) with that `violation_error_code` included in kwargs, so `clone()` reproduces the non-default code; the kwarg is omitted when the code is None (the default).

When FileResponse serves a compressed file whose basename ends in '.br' and no explicit content_type is provided, the response's Content-Type header is set to 'application/x-brotli' (rather than the guessed type such as text/*).

The above cancellation matches purely on the index name (self.index.name == operation.name) without constraining that the paired RemoveIndex targets the same model as the AddIndex or that it immediately follows it, so an AddIndex is also cancelled by a RemoveIndex naming that index even when the two operations name different models and/or have other operations in between.

Elements of the input sequence that are already marked safe (SafeString/SafeData instances or objects exposing an HTML representation via `__html__`) are included in the returned list unchanged with no double-escaping applied.

When serializing in pk format (serializer invoked without natural keys) an object that has an auto-created many-to-many field whose target model's default manager carries a select_related on its queryset, the XML serializer (django.core.serializers.xml_serializer.Serializer) succeeds in iterating the m2m relations and emits one <object pk=...> reference per related object, rather than raising the 'Field ... cannot be both deferred and traversed using select_related at the same time' error.

When _wrap_in_tex converts its input text into TeX math-mode wrapping (used for usetex-rendered date tick labels), every colon ':' character that survives the earlier letter-classification step is braced as '{:}' in the returned string, so that time separators are not typeset with the wide spacing TeX gives to binary/relation operators.

On exit of the matplotlib.rc_context context manager, rcParams['backend'] is left untouched: whatever backend value (or resolution of the auto-backend sentinel) is in effect at the end of the context body is preserved after the context exits, rather than being restored to its value at context entry. In particular, an auto-backend sentinel present in the global rcParams at context entry is never re-installed into rcParams['backend'] by the context's cleanup, and a backend set or resolved inside the body (e.g. by figure creation, by the supplied fname/rc, or by matplotlib.use) is not rolled back.

When a Figure is pickled via __getstate__, the dpi value stored in the resulting pickled state under the '_dpi' key is the figure's original dpi (the '_original_dpi' recorded on its canvas when it was created) rather than the figure's current, possibly device-pixel-ratio-inflated dpi; consequently any inflation of the figure's dpi caused by HiDPI/Retina device-pixel-ratio scaling is discarded on pickling and not carried into the unpickled figure.

For a DraggableBase instance d, d.canvas returns the canvas of d.ref_artist.figure (i.e. d.ref_artist.figure.canvas), resolved dynamically at access time rather than captured once at construction, so that .canvas still evaluates correctly (resolving to the re-attached figure's canvas) after the helper has been unpickled and re-attached to a figure; reads of self.canvas used for supports_blit checks, callback (dis)connection and canvas redraw/blit continue to work.
When one Text's visual properties are copied into another Text via `update_from`, the destination also copies the source's per-instance antialiased value.

When `.subfigures(ncols>1, wspace=w, ...)` is called on a Figure or SubFigure whose layout engine is None (get_layout_engine() returns None) and an explicit non-None wspace is passed, the bounding boxes of the returned column subfigures are adjusted so that a horizontal separation is left between adjacent columns (the grid cells are shrunk to accommodate the wspace gap) rather than every column adjoined flush against the next at the grid width-ratio boundary.

Calling twinx() on an Axes whose x-axis has units set returns a new twin Axes whose xaxis.units equals the calling Axes' self.xaxis.units (i.e. the parent x-axis unit configuration is carried onto the shared horizontal axis of the returned twin).

Constructing an OffsetFrom from a ref_coord that is a numpy array does not alias the caller's array: OffsetFrom stores a value copy of ref_coord, so that later in-place mutation of the passed ref_coord array after construction does not affect the offset transform returned by OffsetFrom.__call__.

The nominal auto axis-limit set described above is applied with matplotlib autoscaling disabled for that axis (auto=None), so that the displayed bounds covering all categories are final and are not updated by later autoscale calls or further data on the axis.

For continuous scales whose major formatter does not expose the set_useOffset/set_scientific controls (e.g. a formatter type lacking these methods), the legend tick labels are left formatted exactly as before — the offset/scientific suppression is applied only when the formatter actually supports it.

Blueprint.__init__ raises ValueError with message "'name' may not be empty." when its name argument is falsy (e.g. an empty string), rather than allowing the Blueprint to be constructed only to misbehave later during registration/endpoint generation.

prepend_scheme_if_needed preserves userinfo/authentication credentials embedded in the input URL across scheme prepending: when the URL's auth component (as parsed by urllib3's parse_url) is non-empty, the returned URL's authority (netloc, reconstructed via urlunparse) includes 'auth@' prefixed onto the host[:port] so the credentials are not dropped from the result.

xr.where(cond, x, y, keep_attrs=True) where y is a Dataset and x is not a Dataset (x is promoted so the result is a Dataset): the result's top-level .attrs is set to {} (not to x.attrs), and the data variable of the result named by x.name, if x has a name present in the result's data_vars, is given x's attrs.

pylint.exports a module-level Boolean constant `IS_PYPY` in `pylint.constants` that is True exactly when the running Python implementation is PyPy (as reported by `platform.python_implementation()`), and False otherwise.

When get_unpacked_marks is called on a class with consider_mro=False, it returns only the marks declared directly on that class (its own pytestmark in its __dict__) and excludes any marks inherited from super-classes.

The single effective copy_X value resolved for a LassoLarsIC.fit call (explicit argument if given, else the estimator's copy_X attribute) is applied consistently to both the data preprocessing step (LinearModel._preprocess_data) and the lars_path call, so that whether the caller's input X array is copied or modified in place is governed by that one resolved value rather than being split between the two.

export_text(decision_tree, feature_names=...) builds its internal per-node feature-name list by mapping split-node feature indices to the corresponding provided feature_names entries, while never using the TREE_UNDEFINED sentinel that leaf nodes store as an index into feature_names, so that calling export_text with a single-feature tree (whose leaf nodes store feature == TREE_UNDEFINED == -2) and a length-1 feature_names list completes and returns the text report instead of raising IndexError.

Under the refit=False (aggregation) path of LogisticRegressionCV.fit, when the penalty is not 'elasticnet', each class entry appended to self.l1_ratio_ is the value None (rather than being derived by indexing the internally-degenerate l1_ratios grid, which for non-elasticnet is the single-element [None] used as a dummy). Observable consequence: after fitting a non-elasticnet LogisticRegressionCV with refit=False, self.l1_ratio_ holds None values, matching the refit=True behavior.

SequentialFeatureSelector.fit determines the cross-validation splitting strategy once using a classifier-aware check (classifier=True when the wrapped estimator is a classifier and False otherwise), so any cross-validation-driven validation that depends on classifier vs regressor semantics is resolved identically for all fold usages throughout a single fit.

roc_curve returns a `thresholds` array whose first element (the extra point added so the curve starts at fpr=0, tpr=0) is exactly `np.inf`, regardless of the values or magnitude of `y_score` (e.g. even when all scores are probabilities within [0,1], thresholds[0] is inf rather than max(y_score)+1, which was previously > 1 for fraction-scale scores).

The n_init candidate runs of k_means are each initialized from an independent per-run random seed (each run receiving its own fresh RandomState seeded by one element of a pre-sampled seed array drawn from the caller's random_state at the start), rather than from a single shared advancing random stream whose state depends on the sequential execution path, so each of the n_init runs' initialization outcome is the same regardless of whether the calling path is single-job or parallel.

In modify_field_list, for every object type (class or otherwise) under autodoc_typehints_description_target == "all", when an 'rtype' field is appended its body paragraph text is exactly the recorded return-annotation string ('annotations['return']'), not the value of any other annotation.

Catalog.__iter__ yields Message objects whose locations list is sorted ascending by (source, line) — ordered lexicographically by source path and then by line number for a given source (previously the locations were in the insertion order of the underlying metadata entries).

When rendering a C++ signature, a user-defined-literal's literal operator suffix identifier is shown as a (non-emphasised) plain text piece linked through a pending cross-reference whose reftarget is the literal-operator name `operator""IDENT`; correspondingly the description mode string 'udl' becomes acceptable to verify_description_mode so ASTIdentifier.describe_signature can be invoked in that mode.

signature_from_str does not misattribute a default declared on an earlier positional-only parameter to a following, non-defaulted positional-or-keyword parameter: in a signature such as '(a, b=0, /, c)', parameter b keeps default 0 while parameter c in the returned Signature has Parameter.empty as its default (a posonly default must not shift the defaults alignment so that the trailing regular parameter inherits it).

Subscripting a _MockObject instance with a key of any type (not only str; e.g. an int, a type, or another non-string object) returns a new _MockObject subclass rather than raising an error, and the name of the resulting subclass is derived from str(key), i.e. the resulting subclass's __display_name__ equals the enclosing mock's __display_name__ + '.' + str(key).

For a non-http(s), non-'scheme://' link URI whose srcdir-relative file does NOT exist on disk but that matches one of the configured linkcheck_ignore patterns, the linkcheck builder reports status 'ignored' (no network request) instead of 'local'.

When an automodule or autoclass directive is processed, the members explicitly named in a list-valued :private-members: or :special-members: option that are not already in the directive's :members: list are appended to it (so they are selected for member enumeration); this merging is skipped when :members: is given as a bare flag (ALL), and it happens both for ModuleDocumenter and ClassDocumenter.

sphinx.ext.autodoc.importer.get_class_members is no longer called with a ModuleAnalyzer argument; its signature has dropped the trailing 'analyzer' parameter so it now takes exactly (subject, objpath, attrgetter).
Calls to sphinx.ext.autodoc.importer.get_module_members(module) now emit a RemovedInSphinx50Warning deprecation warning (while still returning the computed member list).

For Python object descriptions, the argument (variable name) of a :var:, :ivar:, or :cvar: doc field is rendered as plain literal bold text rather than as a cross-reference of role 'obj'; it no longer produces a pending cross-reference that would be resolved against module- and/or class-scoped Python objects bearing that name, and it is therefore never resolved to a same-named object of unrelated scope nor reported as a missing reference under nitpicky builds.

The '|' delimiter, together with any whitespace surrounding it, is preserved in the rendered output as plain non-reference content between the per-alternative references, rather than being dropped or folded into the reftarget of either neighboring type reference.
The py:property directive accepts a ':classmethod:' flag option; providing it does not raise an unknown-option error.

The Literal-special handling applies only when the rendered base token of the bracketed subscript is exactly the bare name 'Literal' or the dotted 'typing.Literal'; for any other subscript base, value-argument text inside the brackets continues to be handled as ordinary type text (converted to type cross-reference nodes when non-whitespace, as before the patch).

When coth is evaluated on an Add argument for which _peeloff_ipi returns a nonzero periodic part m whose coth(m) is the singleton S.ComplexInfinity, evaluation returns coth(x) where x is the peeled rest, rather than raising an exception.

Binary arithmetic that combines a Poly instance with a non-Poly SymPy Expr operand (e.g. a generator Symbol such as x, or a SymPy number such as S(-2)) is dispatched through the Poly's operator methods and yields a Poly-typed result rather than remaining an unevaluated commutative core Mul/Add. In particular x*Poly(x) evaluates to Poly(x**2, x, domain='ZZ') and S(-2)*Poly(x) evaluates to Poly(-2*x, x, domain='ZZ').

A bareiss pivot-candidate entry that is still non-zero (i.e. not recognizably zero after expand_mul, such as an unevaluated bare symbol or float) continues to be selectable as a pivot exactly as when the topmost truthy element was the only choice, so symbolic determinant computations that legitimately used a non-zero pivot still proceed and return a determinant (not zero) — the change only alters the handling of entries that expand to zero.

Add.is_zero (the _eval_is_zero handler) returns None rather than False for an Add belonging to a commutative (real-valued or complex-valued sum) whose classified arguments contain no real term known to be nonzero but contain at least one imaginary-direction term (an argument with is_imaginary, or whose product with the imaginary unit I is real), with any real arguments being individually known-zero; i.e. an expression whose real part is established as zero but whose full zero-ness (whether the imaginary part cancels) is not decidable is reported as unknown (None), not as nonzero (False).

In the Add branch of _sqrt_match, the shortcut that delegates the expression to split_surds (returning split_surds' [a, b, r]) is taken only when the square of every addend is Rational AND positive; an Add whose addends' squares are all Rational but with at least one square non-positive (zero or negative) no longer takes that shortcut.

nthroot_mod(a, n, p) no longer raises NotImplementedError for composite (non-prime) modulus p with n != 2; instead it returns the sorted list of all distinct solutions x in [0, p) to x**n ≡ a (mod p), regardless of the all_roots flag.

In _print_Mul's unequal-fraction handling, a commutative denominator factor that is a Pow whose exponent is exactly -1 and whose base has more than one argument is parenthesized in the printed output when that base is itself a Pow (e.g. base = a**b), the same way bases that are a Mul already are. Concretely, an unevaluated product such as Mul(x, Pow(a**b, -1, evaluate=False)) prints its denominator 'a**b' wrapped in parentheses rather than unwrapped, so the affected term appears with surrounding parentheses in the rendered string.

When itermonomials is called in the integer (total-degree) form with any non-commutative variable present, a candidate monomial is yielded iff its total degree (the sum over its variable factors of their exponents) is at least min_degree — i.e. retained on the summed per-variable exponents rather than on whether any individual variable's exponent reaches min_degree.

When parse_expr is called with evaluate=False, an expression containing the Python '<=' comparison operator is parsed into an unevaluated instance of the SymPy relational class Le (Le(visited_left, visited_right, evaluate=False)) with the parsed operands, rather than being eagerly evaluated to a boolean.
